title: Restriction of Settlement Geography, technique T0142
content: Restriction of Settlement Geography Colonial authorities often impose legal or administrative bans on settling in places of traditional residence or on resettlement. This practice is used to prevent the Indigenous population from accessing resources important to the colonizers, e.g., rivers; to force the Indigenous population into emigration due to the absence of economic and social prospects and the high cost of housing; to create conditions for the migration of groups preferred by the empire to the new territories; and, finally, to reduce the capacity for organized resistance. ID: T0142 ⓘ Tactics: Defense Impairment, Extraction of Benefits, Persistence ⓘ People: Nokhchi (Chechens) Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.0 Created: 18 May 2026 Last Modified: 18 May 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1631 C1117 Police Registration and Restriction of Settlement (1631–1640) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0024 Police Apparatus The metropole's occupation administration legally prohibited the free residence of the Indigenous population in Tersky Town, organizing the forced expulsion of unapproved persons and total demographic control: in 1631, Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich issued a decree to the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace ordering a census of the newly arrived Nokhchi (Michkizians and Okochans) and ruling that those of them «who cannot be trusted» must be «ordered to be expelled out of Tersky Town, and ordered to go back whence each had come»[1]; to ensure surveillance, in the state register of serving people for the region of the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace for 1637, the central authorities recorded in detail the number of subordinate residents of Tersky Town, including 350 «Okotsky people» and 680 newly arrived «Okochans, and Tatars, and Michkizians, and Shibutians»[2]; and in 1640, on the orders of the Terek voivode, the Terek syn boyarsky P. Lukin and the clerk F. Belkov compiled a name-by-name register of the population of the Terek slobodas, rigidly recording every household of the subordinate Nokhchi (Okochans)[1][2]. July 1819 C1143 Demonstrative destruction of the aul of Dadi-Yurt and the erection of the Vnezapnaya fortress to force the Nokhchi off the Kumyk plain (1819) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The Russian Empire drove the Nokhchi from the lowland to clear it for itself and for loyal neighbors, and blocked their return with fortresses. Historian D. A. Khozhaev cites the admission of General Orbeliani that this expulsion was a system applied everywhere: "in all of Chechnya there remained not a single aul, not a single household, that had not been resettled from one place to another several times over"[3]. General Yermolov himself, in a report to the emperor, admits this with regard to the Kachkalyk Nokhchi: to clear the Aksai riverside he drove them out of it and placed the fortresses of Amir-Adzhi-Yurt and Vnezapnaya in their place, for the sake of "freeing it [the Aksai] from the Kachkalyks, whom I immediately ordered to be driven out of it; I established the fortress of Vnezapnaya"[4]. November 1838 C1164 Forcing Chechnya into submission after the fall of Akhulgo and suppression of the general uprising of 1840 (1838-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The "Conditions prescribed to submitting highlanders", issued by general Grabbe, commander of the troops of the Caucasus Line (the chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), on 15 June 1840, forbade the Chechens to choose freely where to live. Point 5 prescribed: "Not to move from one aul to another for permanent residence without the permission of the local authorities"[5]. The right to live on their own land, where they had lived for generations, the empire turned into a permit issued by the authorities. June 1840 C1165 "Constriction of Chechnya from all sides": blockade, secret war, punitive expeditions and the Sunzha Line (1840-1846) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The Terek-side Chechens (inhabitants of the left bank of the Terek) who had fled to the insurgents the empire deprived forever of the right to return home. The "Report of the chancellery for the administration of peaceable highlanders" (not earlier than July 1841) records the directive: "to announce to the fugitive Chechens that they have forever lost the right to settle in the places they occupied before their flight"[5]; lieutenant-colonel Bekovich-Cherkassky (of a Kabardian ruling family, in Russian service, set over the Terek-side auls) "was instructed not to receive Chechens returning from flight without permission"[5]. By that time the houses of the twelve villages had been dismantled and carried off to the Cossack stanitsas - there was nowhere to return to, and returning was forbidden. The programme for the conquest of Chechnya approved by emperor Nicholas I in 1843 prescribed where and how the Chechens were permitted to live. War minister Chernyshev, in a report to the emperor of 16 November 1843, recorded the will of Nicholas I: to permit the Chechens to resettle on the right bank of the Sunzha near the imperial fortifications "not otherwise than in large auls, to adapt them somewhat independently for defence and for the more convenient keeping of the inhabitants in obedience, bearing in mind also in course of time to turn them into the Cossack estate. The left bank of the Sunzha and the expanse up to the Terek are designated for the establishment of Cossack stanitsas and their supply with land"[5]. The norm fixed a double dispossession: the Chechens were allowed to live by their own rivers only in large auls under the guns of the fortifications, while the left bank of the Sunzha up to the Terek was signed over to the Cossacks. The surviving inhabitants of Lesser Chechnya the empire resettled onto the plain under the guns of the fortifications being built. Vorontsov, viceroy and commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, in a report of summer 1846 recorded the course and the hitch of the policy: "The resettlement of the inhabitants of Lesser Chechnya onto the plain near the fortification under construction does not yet have proper success"[5]. By August 1846 resettlers were already living by fort Achkhoy - it was among them that the families of the Chechen Topi, who had promised to serve the empire as a secret scout in the mountains and a guide for its troops, were permitted to settle[5]. The choice of where to live was replaced by assignment: to live by the fortification, in view of the garrison. January 1847 C1166 "Death sentence" for Lesser Chechnya: the massacre of Duba's hamlet, forest clearings, fortresses, annihilation of the population and stanitsas on the sites of burned auls (1847-1851) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The colonization of the Sunzha Line (the chain of Cossack stanitsas along the Sunzha river) left the Chechen people a small part of its own land. Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov sum up: "after the creation of the Sunzha Cossack line and other numerous military fortifications, the greater part of the country's population found itself herded onto a space roughly 70 versts from west to east and 40 versts from south to north" (a verst is slightly more than a kilometer); per person there was less than 2 desiatinas of land (a desiatina is slightly more than a hectare) against a survival norm of 5[6]. Still earlier the empire took on the very order of settlement: "as early as the 1840s the Russian authorities strove to liquidate the numerous hamlets on the territory of lowland Chechnya, forcing their inhabitants to resettle into large villages with the aim of easing the collection of taxes and tributes and ensuring proper police control over the population"[6]. January 1858 C1022 Muhajirism: the expulsion of Chechens to the Ottoman Empire, the ban on return, and population replacement (1858-1872) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The empire's answer to the pleas of those who returned was fixed in a formula "at the very highest level": "Of any return migration of the highlanders there can be no talk"[6]. Under the rules approved in June 1861 by the chief of the Main Staff of the Caucasus Army, General Kartsov, highlanders who had entered Turkish subjecthood or overstayed their passports were "resolutely forbidden" to return[7]. By November 1865, 2,600 people had gathered at the border, ready to accept Orthodoxy for the sake of returning - "However, the Russian leadership even on such terms was in no hurry to let them through the border... they no longer had anywhere to return to; their ancestral lands had been either confiscated or sold"[7]. Those who tried to return secretly were caught for years: in 1867, 162 people were detained; in 1868 - 663; in 1869 - 369; in 1870 - 1,263; "Over ten years, from 1862 to 1872, 5,964 highlanders (mostly Chechens) managed to return to the Terek oblast, of whom 2,315 the authorities forcibly expelled to Turkey once again"[6]. Even those permitted were not allowed home: the returning Karabulaks (a Vainakh society kindred to the Chechens) "were not admitted to their native lands, but settled as a single aul, Sagopshi, on the lands of the Chechen village of Psedakh"[6]. April 1858 C1170 "Military-Popular Administration": the Colonial Regime of the Terek Oblast (1858-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations As early as 1880, by decree of the viceroy, all highlanders were expelled from the Shatoy sloboda - "owing to the decrease of Russians in the sloboda" - with a ban on settling there henceforth[8]. On 14 May 1893 the eviction of highlanders from the towns and slobodas of the oblast began; the bans were lifted piecemeal over decades: for Grozny - on 18 March 1901, for the Vozdvizhenskaya sloboda - on 27 February 1906, for Vedeno and Shatoy - only on 10 May 1916[8]. The head of the oblast justified the repeal not by the rights of the evicted - he petitioned for the repeal of the law of 14 May 1893 as one "serving as a brake on the Russification of the tribes"[8]. By order of 26 August 1898 the head of the garrison of the Shatoy fortification banned entry into the fortification without a bilet - the population of three uchastoks was left without access to the post and telegraph office, the savings bank and the pharmacy[8]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Кушева Е. title: Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back, technique T0039
content: Collusion with a Third Party Behind the People's Back Aggressors may conclude secret or open diplomatic agreements with other geopolitical players on the division of spheres of influence, completely ignoring the sovereignty and interests of the Indigenous people. This technique is used for diplomatic preparation for seizure and the subsequent seizure of governance. Deals made behind the back of the colonized society allow the aggressor to deprive it of potential international allies, legitimize the occupation at the foreign-policy level, and dismember the territories of the local population unimpeded. ID: T0039 ⓘ Tactics: Seizure of Governance, Preparation for Seizure ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: October 1656 C0002 Truce of Vilna (1656) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy As soon as political interests changed, Moscow went for a separate peace with its recent enemy – Poland – negotiating behind its Ukrainian ally's back: "The priorities at the negotiations were territorial and financial questions, as well as the terms of the election of the Russian tsar to the Polish throne"[1] – the fate of the Cossack lands became a bargaining chip in this deal. The negotiations were held at Niemieza near Vilna from August 1656; the armistice was signed on October 24[1]. January 1667 C0005 Truce of Andrusovo (1667) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The official partition of Ukrainian lands between two neighboring states. The treaty was signed exclusively by representatives of Moscow and Warsaw: "Concluded on January 30 (February 9) in the village of Andrusovo, near Smolensk, for 13.5 years. The Russian delegation was headed by okolnichy A. L. Ordin-Nashchokin, the Polish one by commissioner Yu. Hlebowicz"[2]. The opinion of the autonomy itself was completely ignored: "The interests of the hetmans and of Ukraine were, of course, not taken into account"[3]. A separate knot of the collusion was Kyiv: article 7 of the Andrusovo treaty (30 January 1667) stipulated that "the very city of Kyiv… is to be handed over and vacated… that is, within two years, counting from the present treaty… in the coming year 1669, on the 15th day of April"[4]; "Muscovy then did not give it back"[5] - and in 1686 it legalized what it had withheld, "paying for Kyiv once more" (see the "Eternal Peace" campaign). The "territory for money" scheme was laid down in the same document: article 34 records Tsar Aleksei's consent to grant "a worthy treasury for the satisfaction of the szlachta exiles… from the part of Ukraine ceded to His Tsarist Majesty's side"[4] - with the sum deferred to future embassies. January 1686 C0009 "Eternal Peace" with Poland (1686) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The division of spheres of influence behind the Ukrainian ally's back, accompanied by a financial deal for territory: under the 1686 treaty Moscow undertook "to count out one hundred forty-six thousand Muscovite rubles and hand them over to the Commonwealth"[6][3][7]. Ukrainian historiography recorded the deal as an ordinary purchase - Hrushevsky: Muscovy "concluded an eternal accord with Poland (paying, in addition, another 146 thousand rubles for Kyiv)"[5]. January 1699 C0026 Liquidation of the Cossacks in Right-Bank Ukraine (1699) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The backroom partition of Ukraine along the Dnipro: by the "Eternal Peace" of 1686 Moscow officially ceded the Right Bank to Warsaw, without the participation or consent of Ukrainians themselves. The fate of the Right-Bank Cossacks was decided by foreign capitals: the ban of 1699 implemented this partition, against which Palii's Cossacks, "contrary to the terms of the 'Eternal Peace' of 1686," continued the struggle to unite both banks[8]. January 1708 C1126 Suppression of the Uprising of Murat Kuchukov and Terror against the Indigenous Population (1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The diplomatic apparatus of the Tsardom of Muscovy concluded an alliance agreement with Kalmyk forces for joint actions against the Indigenous population: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that on September 30, 1708, "at the negotiations between Peter's military commander P.M. Apraksin and the Kalmyk khan Ayuka, an agreement of eight articles was concluded, including 'on the pursuit of the Chechens and Nogais'"[9]. January 1711 C0027 Pylyp Orlyk's Campaign in Right-Bank Ukraine (1711) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The collapse of the anti-Moscow coalition from within: on the Right Bank, the Tatar allies betrayed the Cossacks and turned to seizing the civilian population – "the Tatars, disobeying Orlyk, scattered in raiding parties and began taking yasyr captives across Ukrainian villages"[10]. Orlyk himself wrote to the Swedish king: "What atrocities unheard of under the moon did the wild Tatars then commit!"[10]. January 1718 C1128 Plundering Expeditions of Cossacks and Allied Princes (1718–1721) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The diplomatic apparatus of the Tsardom of Muscovy used loyal elites of neighboring peoples for joint armed actions against the Nokhchi societies: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that in 1718 an expedition into the lands of the Nokhchi was carried out by the forces of "Kabardian princes allied with Peter I"[9]. January 1722 C1129 Suppression of the Uprising, Military Intervention, and Forced Formalization of Subjecthood (1722) G0009 Russian Empire S0009 Diplomacy The diplomatic apparatus of the Russian Empire enlisted loyal forces of neighboring peoples for joint armed actions against the Nokhchi societies: historian Sh. B. Akhmadov states that the 1722 military expedition included "an armed detachment of Kalmyks, sent by Ayuka Khan at the tsar's request, numbering 3,730 men"[11]. January 1768 C0032 Russo-Turkish War and the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca (1768–1774) G0009 Russian Empire S0009 Diplomacy The signing of the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca: the diplomatic severing of Crimea from the Ottoman Empire through fictitious "independence" – "neither the Russian court nor the Ottoman Porte shall interfere in the election and elevation of the said khan, nor in their domestic, political, civil, and internal affairs under any pretext"[12] – in preparation for the subsequent annexation. January 1793 C0037 Second and Third Partitions of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (1793–1795) G0009 Russian Empire S0009 Diplomacy The diplomatic collusion of the great powers behind the backs of the peoples of the dismembered republic: "Russia carried out the second partition of Poland jointly with Prussia"[8]; all three monarchies took part in the third – the fate of the Right Bank was decided in St. Petersburg, Berlin, and Vienna. June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy The signing of the Treaty of Riga in March 1921: a backroom division of spheres of influence and Ukrainian territories with Poland behind the back of the Ukrainian people, legalized through the formal participation of the puppet Ukrainian SSR[13]. September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0009 Diplomacy The partition of Eastern Europe behind the backs of its peoples: the secret protocol established that "in the event of a territorial-political rearrangement of the areas belonging to the Polish state, the boundary of the spheres of interest of Germany and the USSR shall run approximately along the line of the rivers Narew, Vistula, and San"[14]. Half a century later the Congress of People's Deputies of the USSR "recognizes the secret protocols as legally untenable and invalid from the moment of their signing"[15]. The invasion was covered by Molotov's note to the Polish ambassador Grzybowski (17 September 1939): "the Polish state and its government have in fact ceased to exist"[16]. January 1944 C0084 Suppression of UPA Resistance and Operation "Vistula" (1944–1951) G0010 USSR S0009 Diplomacy The coordination of actions with the pro-Soviet government of Poland to destroy the Ukrainian underground: Operation "Vistula," "as a deportation action, was elaborated in detail and carried out by the Polish authorities," but its execution "was coordinated with the party-Soviet organs of power of the USSR" - the Soviet command transferred "from Lviv oblast one tank division and special NKVD units, and blocked the Ukrainian-Polish border with border troops"[1]. April 2008 C0098 Diplomatic Attack Against NATO Enlargement (2008) G0011 Russian Federation S0009 Diplomacy An attempt to strike a deal with the US leader over Kyiv's head in order to block Ukraine's Euro-Atlantic integration under the threat of its dismemberment: Ukraine's accession to NATO would create "a field of conflict for you and us, long-term confrontation," while Moscow, relying on anti-NATO forces, "would be working on stripping NATO of the possibility of enlarging. Russia would be creating problems there all the time"[17]. As retold by Kommersant's source from the summit itself: "You understand, George, that Ukraine is not even a state! What is Ukraine? Part of its territory is Eastern Europe, and part - a considerable part - was gifted by us!" - with a transparent hint "that Russia could begin the severance of Crimea and Eastern Ukraine"[18]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Редкол.: В. title: Dehumanization, technique T0006
content: Dehumanization Aggressors may use propaganda practices to strip members of the colonized people of their human features. The victim is deliberately marked with derogatory labels (e.g., "subhumans," "militants," "Nazis," "fascists," "terrorists"), which is intended to remove psychological and moral barriers among the occupation troops and to legitimize any atrocities in the eyes of the aggressor's society, leading to a complete loss of empathy. ID: T0006 ⓘ Tactic: Legitimization of Domination ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1721 C1108 Imposition of an Image of Backwardness and the “Civilizing” Mission (1721–1800s) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The government of the Russian Empire deliberately constructed an image of the Indigenous population as criminal savages: historian Michael Khodarkovsky records that in administration documents the highlanders were labeled as "inconstant and treacherous," while their actions were explained by references to their "predatory craft, to which they are predisposed by their very nature and upbringing"[1]. January 1800 C1106 Propagandistic Inversion of Roles and Dehumanization (1800–1864) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The apparatus of the Russian Empire constructed an image of the Indigenous population as savages: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov points out that pre-revolutionary historiography described the highlanders' struggle as «the actions of barbarians devoid of 'civilized' notions of independence and freedom»[2], while the imperial historian and participant in the events V. A. Potto cites the words of General A. P. Yermolov, who declared that «the cruelty of the local mores cannot be tamed by mercy»[3]. In his «Notes», General Yermolov wrote of the Nokhchi: «the Chechens, the most vicious of the brigands, attacking the line», their land a refuge where «the villains of all other peoples, abandoning their own land on account of some crimes, were received amicably», while Chechnya itself «may justly be called the nest of all brigands», «were less filled than others with brigands who had previously taken part in all the raids of the Chechens on the line. In them predators gathered and took cover…»[4]. January 1858 C1022 Muhajirism: the expulsion of Chechens to the Ottoman Empire, the ban on return, and population replacement (1858-1872) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The Viceroy of the Caucasus and commander-in-chief of the Caucasus Army Baryatinsky - on the Chechens who wished to leave: "...it is perhaps no bad thing that all this rabble, which is only a burden to us, will leave. Do not stop them, let them go to Mecca or wherever they wish. And I will take care to present this matter to the Sovereign in the proper light..." - to the emperor the matter was presented as "a voluntary movement of the Chechens themselves"[5]. The head of the Kuban oblast, General Yevdokimov, who carried out the expulsion of the highlanders of the Western Caucasus, formulated the principle: "Philanthropy first of all to our own; as for the highlanders, I consider myself entitled to grant them only what remains for their share after the last of Russian interests has been satisfied"[5]. The optic in which such decisions were taken was also articulated by imperial scholarship: Berzhe, who headed the Caucasus Archaeographic Commission for 22 years and compiled the first ten volumes of the "Acts"[6], grounded distrust of the highlanders in their nature: "The eight-hundred-thousand-strong highland population of the Terek and Dagestan oblasts forms here an almost solid mass... Permeated by Muslim fanaticism, inflamed by the long war, it continues to hate us as still-recent sworn enemies, as infidels, and will preserve this feeling as long as we remain giaours in its eyes"[7]. This is not an order but the voice of the epoch - the language in which the expulsion looked natural. July 1925 C1177 The disarmament of Chechnya: a military operation with artillery shelling and bombing of auls (1925) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army On 31 July 1925 the Revolutionary Military Council of the USSR explained the operation being prepared by the properties of an entire people - the order says: "The Chechen oblast is a hotbed of criminal banditry spreading to the districts neighboring Chechnya... In their mass the Chechens are inclined to banditry as the main source of easy gain, which is furthered by the presence of a large quantity of weapons. Mountain Chechnya is a refuge for the most hardened enemies of Soviet power"[8]. The label from the order passed into the operation's working nomenclature: the instruction of 4 August 1925, approved by Uborevich, commander of the North Caucasus Military District, Volodin, member of the district's Revolutionary Military Council, and Yevdokimov, plenipotentiary representative of the OGPU (the political police, a predecessor of today's FSB) for the krai, puts people in one row with rifles and "removes" them with a single verb - point 8 of the instruction reads: "If the conditions of the surrender of weapons are fulfilled, no house-to-house search is conducted, and only the bandit and vicious element is removed"[9]. Thus criminality was declared a property of the people, and its men - an "element" subject to removal. September 2004 C0096 Election Interference and Countering the "Orange Revolution" (2004) G0011 Russian Federation S0021 Propaganda The conduct of an aggressive information campaign in favor of "their" candidate with the direct participation of the head of the Russian state: live on three Ukrainian television channels two weeks before the vote, praise was voiced for the candidate's government - "V. Yanukovych's government achieved more: they managed to fill this growth with good quality. That is, Ukraine's economy is developing in a diversified way"[10]. In parallel, opponents were demonized with accusations of nationalism and pro-fascist views. January 2020 C0102 Ideological Preparation for the Full-Scale Invasion (2020–2021) G0011 Russian Federation S0009 Diplomacy An article by D. Medvedev, deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, in Kommersant (11 October 2021) marginalizing the Ukrainian leadership: "it is pointless for us to deal with vassals. One must do business with the suzerain"; "at the head of Ukraine stand weak people who strive only to line their own pockets," and negotiations with them are "absolutely pointless"[11]. In the same text the Ukrainian president was likened to a hypothetical Jew serving in the SS[11]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Michael Khodarkovsky. Медведев, «Коммерсантъ», 11 октября 2021. (2021). Почему бессмысленны контакты с нынешним украинским руководством.

title: Imposition of a Backwardness Narrative, technique T0001
content: Imposition of a Backwardness Narrative Aggressors may systematically disseminate a narrative that the culture, way of life, and social organization of an Indigenous people are primitive and undeveloped. Constructing an image of backwardness serves the legitimization of domination, making it possible to justify occupation and repression with the fabricated necessity of bringing progress and "civilization." ID: T0001 ⓘ Tactic: Legitimization of Domination ⓘ People: Nokhchi (Chechens) Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1721 C1108 Imposition of an Image of Backwardness and the “Civilizing” Mission (1721–1800s) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The government of the Russian Empire justified expansion with ideas of enlightening undeveloped societies: historian Michael Khodarkovsky states the ambition of the metropole's officials "to bring both Christianity and civilization to the 'wild and uncivilized' peoples along its borders"[1]. July 1925 C1177 The disarmament of Chechnya: a military operation with artillery shelling and bombing of auls (1925) G0010 USSR S0010 Regular Army On 31 July 1925 the Revolutionary Military Council of the USSR, in the order justifying the operation to disarm Chechnya, declared the Chechens incapable of proper farming: "The rich lands granted to the Chechens on the plain after the revolution are not used by them in full; they run their agriculture in backward forms, are not industrious"[2]. The accusation stands in a military order as one of the grounds for sending in troops: the lands were "granted" to the people by the authorities themselves, their way of farming was declared backward by the same authorities, and the conclusion drawn from this assessment was a military operation. Historian T. U. Elbuzdukayeva, who publishes the order, also cites its continuation: "political indications" had ripened - the population's weariness of war and the demand to fight "banditry"[2] - that is, even by the document's own logic the war was to be waged not on economic backwardness, yet it is backwardness that is set down as a justification. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Michael Khodarkovsky. title: Deprivation of Agency, technique T0008
content: Deprivation of Agency Aggressors may deliberately deny an Indigenous people the right to independent political, legal, and historical existence. At the ideological level, this manifests in the dissemination of narratives about the colonized society's lack of agency, which serves the legitimization of domination. At the diplomatic and administrative level, the technique is implemented through the unilateral abolition of sovereignty, the annulment or rewriting of previously concluded international treaties, and the shift of relations from equal footing to a format of direct diktat, which ensures the institutional seizure of governance and the legal consolidation of the occupation. ID: T0008 ⓘ Tactics: Legitimization of Domination, Seizure of Governance, Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1614 C1114 Deprivation of the Nokhchi of political agency and the imposition of alien governance (1614–1616) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The metropole deliberately ignored official complaints by the Indigenous population about the arbitrary conduct of the appointed rulers, depriving them of the right to protection: the compilers of academic document collections state that, as regards the petition submitted to Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich, «the petition of the «Okochans» was not granted»[1]. October 1656 C0002 Truce of Vilna (1656) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The Tsardom of Muscovy physically and legally isolated the autonomy from participation in international politics, deciding the fate of the Cossack lands without regard for their national interests: "The plenipotentiary representatives of the Ukrainian Cossack state, headed by R. Haponenko, were not admitted to the negotiating table"[2]. The hetman's request to grant the envoys mandates as full participants was "let pass unheeded" by the tsar's government: the delegates "sat idle beside the commissioners, not admitted to the official sessions"[3]. January 1667 C0005 Truce of Andrusovo (1667) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy In the legal partition of Ukrainian lands, the opinion of the people themselves or of their leaders was demonstratively ignored. The Hetmanate was treated exclusively as an object: "The interests of the hetmans and of Ukraine were, of course, not taken into account"[4]. January 1686 C0009 "Eternal Peace" with Poland (1686) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy The complete exclusion of the autonomy from participation in international negotiations on the status of its own territories. In the legal partition of Ukrainian lands the opinion of the people themselves was ignored – contemporary Ukrainian historiography assesses the Eternal Peace "as a national tragedy of Ukraine"[4]. January 1687 C0007 Kolomak Articles (1687) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0009 Diplomacy "In this provision of the articles, the tsarist government's aspiration to turn Ukraine into a region incorporated into the Russian state on ordinary terms was openly declared for the first time"[4]. January 1700 C0011 Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government A course toward the complete absorption and destruction of the very name of the Cossack state. In the Bendery Constitution of 1710, Orlyk recorded Moscow's intention "to eradicate the Zaporozhian Host of the Lower Dnipro and to efface its name forever"[5]. Hrushevsky confirms the course was systemic: Mazepa's alliance with the Swedish king merely "gave the Muscovite government occasion… to take up more forcefully the abolition of Ukrainian autonomy. The Muscovite government had pursued this line from the very beginning"[6]. What was at stake was the enslavement of the entire people: the Muscovite state, per the preamble of Orlyk's constitution, managed to "violate and utterly destroy" the rights and liberties "and to cast a slave's yoke upon the free Cossack people, never conquered by it"[7]. June 1709 C0015 The Battle of Poltava and the Final Defeat of the Hetmanate (1709) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government The liquidation of the autonomy's statehood and international agency as a result of the defeat of the Swedish-Ukrainian forces. The rout at Poltava set off an irreversible process of dismantlement: "In the hundred years after the famous Pereiaslav Council, Ukraine traveled the path from the 'Articles of Bohdan Khmelnytsky'… to the de facto liquidation of the autonomy and the hetmanate, to the country's transformation into an ordinary province of the Russian Empire"[5]. July 1709 C0016 The Reshetylivka Articles (1709) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government Refusal to sign a treaty: the replacement of an equal agreement with the tsar's unilateral "resolutions." "The joint document, drawn up as a decree, was signed by state chancellor Count G. Golovkin"[8][9] – the autonomy ceased to be a party to a treaty. January 1728 C0028 The Decisive Points (1728) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government Rejection of the treaty format: instead of a bilateral agreement – the tsar's "decisive" resolutions upon the hetman's requests, issued in the form of a decree. The autonomy ceased to be a party to a treaty and received its rules of existence from above. November 1764 C0030 Liquidation of the Institution of the Hetmancy and the Second Little Russian Collegium (1764) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The final elimination of the office of the autonomy's leader: after Rozumovsky's forced abdication, Catherine II's decree of November 10, 1764 handed power to the Little Russian Collegium, whose president was instructed to act "with a governor's authority, that is, as our special plenipotentiary"[10]. Catherine II's instruction to procurator-general Vyazemsky (1764) stated the goal openly: "and when there is no hetman in Little Russia, one must strive that the very age and name of hetmans vanish"[11]. January 1919 C0074 Second Armed Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0014 White Movement (AFSR) S0009 Diplomacy The refusal of the White commanders to recognize Ukrainian statehood. General Denikin, as commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces of South Russia, signed the programmatic address "To the Population of Little Russia" (August 1919), which declared the struggle for a Ukrainian state to be treason. Symon Petliura (head of the Directory of the Ukrainian People's Republic and chief otaman of its army) and his associates, the address ran, "having begun the dismemberment of Russia, continue even now their evil work of creating an independent 'Ukrainian State' and of fighting against the rebirth of a United Russia"[12]. Denikin wrote in the first person: "declaring Russian the state language throughout the whole expanse of Russia, I consider entirely inadmissible and prohibit the persecution of the Little Russian folk language"[12]. The promised "prohibition of persecution" did not recognize the language but assigned it the place of a vernacular. What remained for Ukrainian under the address were everyday life, private schools, and the first years of primary school - Denikin explained: "to ease the pupils' assimilation of the first rudiments of knowledge"; the "treasonous movement" for statehood he required to be "completely distinguished" from the permitted "love for the native region… and its local folk language"[12]. Denikin allowed the people's existence and denied it political subjecthood: the striving for an independent Ukrainian state was declared treason, the language was left a vernacular. On the night of September 1, 1919, after four hours of negotiations, the Galician general Kravs and Denikin's general Bredov (according to the diary of the Supreme Command of the Ukrainian Galician Army - the commander of the Guards corps) agreed: the Galician units would withdraw from the city that same day "at least beyond the line of the Kyiv railway stations", then to the line Ihnativka - Vasylkiv - Hermanivka, while the Galician army guarantees that it "will make no moves against the army of the volunteers [Denikin's Volunteer Army]"[13]. In the fourth point the Galician command renounced political subjecthood: "The commander of the Kyiv group of the Galician army declares that the Galician army operates independently of Petliura's army under separate Galician command, without any political aims, and solely with the purpose of fighting the Bolsheviks"[13]. A day earlier, on August 30, at negotiations with the command of Denikin's 2nd brigade, its representatives demanded that the territory southeast and east of the Koziatyn - Fastiv - Kyiv railway be treated as "the operational zone of Denikin's troops", and that the strip between the line Fastiv - Volodarka - Saskiv - Buky and the line Bila Tserkva - Tarashcha - Lysivka - Zvenyhorodka be declared neutral; the diary records: "We did not agree to this demand"[13]. June 1919 C0075 Institutional Absorption through a "Military-Political Union" (1919–1921) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0009 Diplomacy De facto liquidation of the Ukrainian army (the disbandment of the Ukrainian Front) and the transformation of the government of the Ukrainian SSR into a nominal appendage of the Russian administrative machine[14]. August 1991 C0094 Diplomatic Blackmail (the "Chicken Kiev" Speech, August 1991) G0010 USSR S0009 Diplomacy The union center deployed an international platform against Ukrainian sovereignty: Bush publicly called the striving for independence a "suicidal nationalism based upon ethnic hatred"[15] – the speech went down in history as the "Chicken Kiev speech." January 2020 C0102 Ideological Preparation for the Full-Scale Invasion (2020–2021) G0011 Russian Federation S0009 Diplomacy The official denial of the Ukrainian nation's right to independent statehood: the article by the head of the Russian state declares outright that "Ukraine's genuine sovereignty is possible precisely in partnership with Russia," while "the wall that has arisen in recent years between Russia and Ukraine" is declared a split of "between parts of what is essentially one historical and spiritual space"[16]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Кушева Е. title: Puppet Government, technique T0037
content: Puppet Government Aggressors may artificially create and install fully controlled organs of power in occupied territories. Forming a puppet government allows the aggressor to simulate an internal civil conflict for the initial seizure of governance, and then to rule the region by proxy for long-term institutional consolidation. ID: T0037 ⓘ Tactics: Seizure of Governance, Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: October 1708 C0012 Mazepa's Defection to Sweden and the Baturyn Massacre (1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army The installation of a government fully controlled by Moscow after the destruction of the capital: the election of the new hetman took place in Peter's presence immediately after the execution of the Baturyn officers – "Under the circumstances, the officers simply confirmed Skoropadsky, presented by Peter"[1]. Hrushevsky records the mechanics of dependence: "The hetman's residence was moved from Baturyn to Hlukhiv, right up against the Muscovite border, and two Muscovite regiments were garrisoned there so that the residents could arrest the hetman and the officers at once," and "everyone in Ukraine understood that power lay not with the hetman but with those residents"[2]. December 1917 C0072 Creation of a Puppet Government and Disguising the Intervention (December 1917 – Early 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The holding of an alternative congress in Kharkiv and the creation of a Moscow-controlled "People's Secretariat" to imitate an internal struggle: it was created "as an alternative to the Ukrainian Central Rada and the General Secretariat of the Ukrainian Central Rada" and "acted in close contact with and under the direct leadership of the highest state and party institutions of Soviet Russia"[3]. The congress declared Ukraine part of Russia. In the resolution on the self-determination of Ukraine, adopted in Kharkiv on 12 (25) December 1917, the congress recognized "the Ukrainian Republic as a federative part of the Russian Republic" and declared "a resolute struggle against the policy of the Central Rada, ruinous for the worker-peasant masses, exposing its bourgeois, counter-revolutionary character"[4]. The congress derived its mandate from the decisions of Petrograd: in the words of the resolution, "the principle of the right of nations to self-determination, proclaimed by the February Revolution, could be brought to life only thanks to the October Revolution, which led to the creation of the Workers' and Peasants' Government — the Council of People's Commissars"[4]. The secretariat's own power came down to another state's decrees: it "announced the overthrow of the UCR and the recognition of only its own decrees as valid. It introduced the decrees of the Council of People's Commissars of Russia in Ukraine"[3][5]. Moscow kept its man inside the government as well: Serhii Bakynskyi, people's secretary for inter-national affairs, was simultaneously "the representative of the CPC of Russia"[3]. Historian Stanislav Kulchytsky describes the direct oversight: "since a Ukrainian party center did not exist, Lenin placed a temporary extraordinary commissar over the Kharkiv government" - Georgii Ordzhonikidze, an official of the central party apparatus[6]. The journal of the Istpart of the CP(b)U "Letopis revoliutsii" wrote in 1924: "The All-Ukrainian government was a center without a periphery, a staff without an army, when it had neither territory, nor a population subordinate to it, nor an armed force"[7]. February 1919 C1174 Denikin's terror in Chechnya: destroyed auls and 15 thousand dead (1919) G0014 White Movement (AFSR) S0010 Regular Army In 1919 General Denikin refused to recognize the Mountain government and dissolved it[8]; General Lyakhov, appointed ruler of the Terek oblast, agreed to regard the republic's parliament as no more than "a consultative organ attached to his person"[9]. As ruler of Chechnya the Volunteer Army appointed a general from among the Chechens - historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "As Ruler of Chechnya on behalf of the Volunteer Army was appointed a well-known military man - General Eriskhan (Iriskhan) Aliev, a Chechen by origin"[9]. On 29 March 1919 Denikin convened a conference in Grozny - as the same historians write, one "called upon to put an end to the bloodshed and to confirm E. Aliev as ruler of Chechnya" - attended by representatives of 42 villages, mostly supporters of the Atagi Soviet (the Chechen National Council, which sat in Starye Atagi), entrepreneurs and part of the clergy[9]. February 2014 C0100 Beginning of the Russo-Ukrainian War: Armed Invasion and Occupation of Crimea (2014) G0011 Russian Federation S0017 Secret Police and Security Services The installation of a controlled administration under military cover: the decisions of the Crimean parliament were taken in conditions where "behind the backs of Crimea's self-defense forces, our servicemen, of course, stood"[10]. The UN General Assembly declared the ensuing referendum void and confirmed that it "was not authorized by Ukraine"[11]. OHCHR recorded the "election" scene itself: overnight into 27 February "armed groups without insignia took over the buildings of the local government and parliament," and "on 27 February, members of the Parliament of Crimea, in the presence of gunmen, dismissed the local Government and elected Sergey Aksenov as the Head of Crimea"[12]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Татьяна Таирова-Яковлева. title: Administrative-Territorial Division, technique T0030
content: Administrative-Territorial Division Aggressors very often alter administrative boundaries within a captured region. In the course of implementing this technique, traditional systems of local governance are forcibly abolished, while the seized lands are fragmented and integrated into the colonizer's standard bureaucratic grid, which irreversibly destroys the historically formed social ties within the society. For example, many borders in Africa are the result of struggles between colonial powers[1]. The borders of the union and autonomous republics of the USSR were established by Moscow for administrative convenience and were changed in accordance with the decisions of the Moscow leadership[2]. ID: T0030 ⓘ Tactic: Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1667 C0005 Truce of Andrusovo (1667) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government The legal codification of the territory's division. Moscow deliberately fragmented a once unified country, turning such important regions as Zaporizhzhia into rightless buffer zones under joint administration: "...Zaporizhzhia (which under the treaty of 1667 was under the joint rule of Moscow and Warsaw)"[3]. January 1686 C0009 "Eternal Peace" with Poland (1686) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government The legal codification of the country's split into two parts, with the Right Bank turned into a buffer zone: "Under the terms of the Eternal Peace, the Right Bank remained with Poland... it was agreed and resolved that those places are to remain deserted, as they now are"[3][4]. January 1699 C0026 Liquidation of the Cossacks in Right-Bank Ukraine (1699) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government The abolition of the regimental-sotnia administrative order to serve the imperial partition of the lands: the Sejm of 1699 adopted the decision "banning the Cossacks on the Right Bank"[5]. January 1700 C0011 Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government Preparation for the liquidation of the Hetmanate through the gubernia reform, into which Cossack towns were artificially inscribed. Moscow planned "to take the Little Russian towns into its own domain"[3][4]. January 1765 C0031 Abolition of the Cossack Order in Sloboda Ukraine (1765) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The liquidation of Cossack administrative units and the introduction of imperial division: the report of the Shakhovskoy-Panin commission confirmed by the empress on December 16, 1764 and Catherine II's manifesto of July 28, 1765[6][7] – "On the basis of the Sloboda regiments the Sloboda-Ukrainian Governorate was formed"[8]. January 1781 C0034 Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The abolition of the Cossack regimental order and the division of the Left Bank into imperial viceroyalties: the Kyiv Viceroyalty was established by the nominal decree to the Senate of September 16, 1781 (PSZRI, coll. 1, vol. XXI, no. 15,228; execution ordered from November)[9][10], "which finally abolished the remnants of the Hetmanate's autonomy and its regimental-sotnia administrative-political and military order"[11]; the same decree established the Chernihiv and Novhorod-Siverskyi viceroyalties. January 1801 C0038 Creation of the Little Russian Governorate-General (1801–1811) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The erasure of historical borders and the introduction of the imperial vertical: "The governor-general concentrated the entire fullness of administrative power: he was endowed with the right of legislative initiative, determined the degree to which all-Russian laws extended within the governorate-general, and controlled the activity of state institutions, including judicial ones"[12]. April 1858 C1170 "Military-Popular Administration": the Colonial Regime of the Terek Oblast (1858-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The oblast was recut in 1862, 1869, 1888 and 1899[13]. From 1 May 1888 the Vedeno and Argun okrugs were merged into the Grozny okrug - under the formula quoted by historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova, "to shield the Cossacks from the 'corrupting' influence of the highlanders"[13]. The Chechen villages on the right bank of the Terek, which were slated for transfer to the Kizlyar and Pyatigorsk otdels (Cossack divisions), were set apart as a special uchastok (sub-district) and temporarily left under the head of the Grozny okrug; the mountain okrugs were divided into uchastoks, while the Cossack otdels were divided by the pattern of manning military units, into sotnias (Cossack hundreds) and regiments[13]. From 1 January 1899 the oblast was recut once more: four otdels - Pyatigorsk, Mozdok, Kizlyar, Sunzha - and four okrugs: Vladikavkaz, Khasav-Yurt, Nalchik, Grozny[13]. January 1918 C0073 Artificial Separatism and the Dismemberment of Territories (January – March 1918) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0008 Government An attempt at the bureaucratic resubordination of territories — declaring the Donbas an autonomous part directly linked to Russia, bypassing any Ukrainian authorities[14]. January 1954 C0087 The Ideological Campaign of the "300th Anniversary of Reunification" and the Transfer of Crimea (1954) G0010 USSR S0008 Government The redrawing of internal borders by the USSR Supreme Soviet Presidium's resolution of 19 February 1954: "To approve the joint submission of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the RSFSR and the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Ukrainian SSR on the transfer of the Crimean oblast from the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic to the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic"[15] – the decision was taken in Moscow, without any expression of will by the peninsula's inhabitants. Behind the "commonality of the economy" stood the desire to shift the peninsula, ruined by deportation and war, onto the books of the Ukrainian SSR: "Moscow admits ever more openly: the Crimean region is a problem territory that the union center does not know how to sustain"[16]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Jack Paine, Xiaoyan Qiu and Joan Ricart-Huguet. title: Expropriation of Resources, technique T0052
content: Expropriation of Resources Aggressors may carry out large-scale and systematic confiscation of natural, financial, and material assets in the captured territory. In the course of implementing this technique, industrial equipment is removed, the treasury is seized, food is confiscated, and mineral resources are exploited without restraint, solely for the extraction of benefits and to meet the needs of the metropole. ID: T0052 ⓘ Tactic: Extraction of Benefits ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1617 C1115 Economic Exploitation and Creation of Dependency of the Nokhchi (1617–1622) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations Representatives of the metropole confiscated the personal property of a deceased Nokhchi delegate into the state treasury: a memorandum from the Posolsky Prikaz to the Prikaz of the Kazan Palace prescribed an investigation into the death of the drowned Okotsky murza Kokhostrov Biytemirov, while of what was found they «took his clothing and all his goods into our treasury»[1]. October 1708 C0012 Mazepa's Defection to Sweden and the Baturyn Massacre (1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army Large-scale looting of state arsenals and the treasury during the punitive raid on the autonomy's capital: "Menshikov managed to remove part of the artillery"[2][3]; the remaining guns were blown up and the city burned. January 1709 C0014 Liquidation of the Zaporozhian Sich (1709) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army Destruction of the military-economic base of the Lower Dnipro Cossacks. The Sich "was a kind of military base housing the fleet, artillery, and arsenal"[4] – all of this infrastructure was destroyed or seized during the assault. January 1781 C0034 Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The secularization and confiscation into the imperial treasury of the lands of Ukrainian Orthodox monasteries: "in 1786, during the secularization, the monastery was closed, and its property and lands passed to the state treasury"[5] – the fate of the Sviatohirsk monastery is typical of the entire 1786 campaign, which deprived the local church of its economic base. August 1832 C1155 Extermination of 61 settlements of lowland Chechnya and mountainous Ichkeria by Rosen's troops, burning alive of the defenders of Germenchuk, and extortion of hostages from 80 villages (1832) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army Following the campaign of August - September 1832, the troops of corps commander Rosen exacted tribute and fines in money and livestock from the Chechen villages: Rosen reported to Minister of War Chernyshev that in total over the campaign "tribute and fines in money and livestock have been paid... about 5 th. r. s. [five thousand rubles in silver]"[6]. November 1838 C1164 Forcing Chechnya into submission after the fall of Akhulgo and suppression of the general uprising of 1840 (1838-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The empire seized the Chechens' property and land by decree. In April 1840 an imperial directive prescribed "to sequester the Aukh herds wherever they are found at pasture in the Kumyk domain" (the Aukhovites - a Chechen community in the north-east, by the Kumyk border)[7]. The land of the Chechens the empire handed out to loyalists: a contemporary's letter from Tiflis, cited by historian N. I. Pokrovsky, names among the causes of the 1840 uprising "the endowment of prince Bekovich-Cherkassky with lands owned by the Chechens" (Bekovich-Cherkassky - a Kabardian prince in Russian service)[8]. June 1840 C1165 "Constriction of Chechnya from all sides": blockade, secret war, punitive expeditions and the Sunzha Line (1840-1846) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army After the inhabitants of twelve Terek-side villages (Chechen settlements of the left bank of the Terek) fled to the insurgents in June 1840, the empire gave their property to the Cossacks. The "Report of the chancellery for the administration of peaceable highlanders", drawn up not earlier than July 1841, lists the villages - Stary Naur, Novy Naur, Emingulovskaya, Murdarova, Boyan-Yurt, Kacherman-Yurt, Nagai Mirza-Yurt, Mizhi-Yurt, Kozhakhi, Kalauzova, Mamakai-Yurt and Guneshki - and records the regime: "the grain left standing in their fields the line Cossacks were permitted... to gather for their own benefit, the houses remaining in the localities to be dismantled and carried off to the stanitsas" (line Cossacks - the Cossack troops of the empire's border line)[7]. The same report records the division of spoils: 800 rams seized by lieutenant-colonel Bekovich-Cherkassky (of a Kabardian ruling family, in Russian service) while pursuing the fleeing inhabitants of Mizhi-Yurt and Kozhakhi "were ordered to be distributed as a reward to those inhabitants of the said two villages who remained devoted to us"[7]. The land taken from the expelled the empire handed over to the Cossack host. Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov record: "to the Cossacks were given in Lesser Chechnya the 'ancestral' lands of the inhabitants of Karabulak and Galashki" (Lesser Chechnya - the lowland-piedmont western part of Chechnya; Galashki - a Vainakh community in the valley of the Assa)[9]. The word "ancestral" comes from the imperial papers themselves: what was being given away was not wasteland but land on which people had lived for generations. February 1845 C1173 Colonial oil: the seizure of the Grozny subsoil and the rent of the Cossack host (1845-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The Russian Empire took the oil wells near the Groznaya fortress away from the Chechens and on 16 February 1845 sealed the seizure by law: paragraph 154 of the "Regulations on the Caucasus Line Host", confirmed by Emperor Nicholas I, read: "as a mark of special favor…the host is granted the income most graciously bestowed upon it from the oil springs near the Groznaya fortress"[10]. Before the seizure the oil fed the Chechens themselves - historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova writes from the documents: in 1788 the Chechen ruler Kazbulat "traded and had a certain income from the oil wells located in his domains"; the Mozdok Cossacks recalled in a petition of 1811 how oil "was brought for sale... and sold at a free price"; "Later, the oil was taken away from the Chechens and became the property of the Caucasus Line regiment, which farmed it out"[10]. Over the 57 years of the tax-farming system, from 1833 to 1890, the host received 152,500 rubles in silver of net income[10][9]. January 1847 C1166 "Death sentence" for Lesser Chechnya: the massacre of Duba's hamlet, forest clearings, fortresses, annihilation of the population and stanitsas on the sites of burned auls (1847-1851) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The land of the evicted communities of Lesser Chechnya (the lowland-piedmont western part of Chechnya) passed to the empire. General Sleptsov, in a report to General Ilyinsky of 4 October 1850, summed up the displacement of the mountain auls: "the rich lands between the Sunzha and the Russian road have passed into the unaccountable possession of the government, so that the entire plain of Lesser Chechnya is now completely cleared of the hostile population"[11]. "Unaccountable possession" is the report's own formula: the land was taken without any registration of the former owners' rights. January 1852 C1167 "Neither plow nor sow": the pogrom of Chechnya, organized famine, the buying-up of elites and the institutions of subjugation (1852-1857) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The clearings took from the Chechens the land that fed them, and the empire entered this seizure on its books: the order of Vorontsov, viceroy in the Caucasus, for the Separate Caucasus Corps of 5 January 1853 counted the result of the Qachqalyq clearing: "The construction of this clearing took away from the unsubdued Chechens a significant quantity of land, which could feed up to 1,500 souls"[11]. January 1860 C1171 Land plunder: the colonial repartition of land, land hunger and Cossack colonization of the Terek oblast (1860-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations According to the summary by historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov, of the 643 thousand desiatinas (a desiatina is a little over a hectare) of lowland and piedmont Chechnya, Chechen villages were left 347 thousand, Cossack stanitsas were handed 222 thousand - a third, officers as private owners got 28 thousand, fortifications 17 thousand, and the treasury about 30 thousand desiatinas of "reserve" land[9]. The same partition was described by the office itself: the Terek land-survey administration, counting only the lowland part of Greater and Lesser Chechnya (a narrower scope than the lowland and piedmont Chechnya of the historians' summary), summed up: "The entire lowland part of Greater and Lesser Chechnya, with the adjoining Lesser-Chechen forest, comprises an area of 271086 desiatinas. Of it, at various times, 650 desiatinas went to 6 Cossack stanitsas, 1560 desiatinas of forest to the Terek Cossack Host, 8645 desiatinas were granted into private ownership for the services of individual persons, 8266 desiatinas were given to towns and settlements, 234970 desiatinas were allotted to 43 Chechen auls, and 16965 desiatinas were held by the forestry department. Thus, there is no free land left…"[10]. The forests were confiscated wholesale: "in Chechnya and Ingushetia tsarism appropriated forests with a total area of 225.5 thousand desiatinas (they became 'state' forests) and handed another 33.5 thousand desiatinas along the Sunzha and its tributaries to the Cossack host. The forests were placed under armed guard, and the unfortunate peasants caught felling wood were pursued with heavy penalties"[9]. From the mountain auls, according to historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova, "50989 desiatinas of pasture were confiscated to the treasury", and the same pastures were then handed back to the communities "on terms of quitrent use"[10]. What people had cleared with their own hands was taken too: in 1874 in the Vedeno okrug the owners of 250 desiatinas of plots cleared from under forest were told to swear on the Quran that the clearing had been done with the permission of the communities - "in the whole okrug only Sh. Dolatmurzayev, a resident of the village of Belgatoy, was able to swear... all the other plots, whose owners to their honor did not risk giving a false oath, were declared communal"[9]; after the uprising of 1877 the residents of Dyshni-Vedeno had 74 certificates for cleared plots taken away "as punishment, for support of the insurgents"[10]. In 1888 the Chechen communities petitioned the emperor: building materials and firewood they were "forced to buy from private owners or from the treasury, whereas formerly they had used them free of charge"[10]. In 1891 the Vladikavkaz Railway Company received a concession for a branch line from Beslan station through Grozny to Petrovsk[12]. On 15 June 1891 Alexander III, by a personal decree to the Minister of Ways of Communication, ordered the expropriation of land for the route: "Having authorized the construction of the Petrovsk railway, in place of its previously indicated direction from Vladikavkaz to Petrovsk, along the direction from Beslan station... to Petrovsk, we command: 1) that the proper arrangements be made for the expropriation... of the lands necessary for this purpose"[13]. The trackbed, the station and the entire railway infrastructure landed on lands that by then were registered to the Terek Cossack Host and the Groznenskaya stanitsa - the very lowland land that had been taken from Chechen auls and handed to the host: historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write that "the railway trackbed (and, accordingly, the station and all the railway facilities) passed over lands belonging to the Terek Cossack Host", and "the Grozny city railway station was built on the land of the Groznenskaya stanitsa"[9]. The bargaining over the price went on between the railway, the town and the Cossacks: the town authorities demanded "60 rubles for every square sazhen of town land expropriated for the construction of the station, the locomotive depot with workshops, the goods station and the access tracks", while the Cossacks of the Groznenskaya stanitsa offered the builders their plot free of charge - counting on oil-refining and other enterprises rising around the station[9]. The money for the expropriation went to the holders of what had been seized; the Chechen communities had no part in that settlement. June 1860 C1169 Suppression of the 1860-1861 uprisings, the execution of Baysangur, and the shooting of the zikrists near Shali (1860-1864) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army A report of 6 August 1860 from the commander of the Caucasus Army to the Minister of War records, concerning the deported Akkins: "the land they occupied has been declared state property, and thus the matter of the Akkins has been settled conclusively"[14]. The historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov confirm: the inhabitants of the Akki society "were dispersed over the course of July among the Galash and other neighboring societies. The land of the Akki society was thereby declared 'state property'"[9]. April 1877 C1172 "Mow Down Everything, Beat and Hang Without Mercy": Suppression of the 1877 Uprising and the Executions in Grozny (1877-1878) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army Following the suppression of the 1877 uprising the empire took away the land of the mountain communities: historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova records - "Thousands of inhabitants of mountain villages were resettled onto the plain; their lands were confiscated"[10]. January 1919 C0074 Second Armed Invasion and Resource Depletion (1919) G0013 Soviet Russia (RSFSR) S0010 Regular Army Forcible requisitioning ("prodrazverstka") and the non-stop export of grain, coal, and raw materials to the RSFSR without economic compensation, which provoked uprisings, among them Hryhoriv's[15]. January 1928 C0077 Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services Mass dispossession and forced deportation of hundreds of thousands of resisting peasants (the so-called "kurkuls") to remote special settlements in Siberia and the North[15]. June 1941 C0082 Scorched Earth Tactics and Criminal Mobilization (1941–1945) G0010 USSR S0008 Government The total removal of industrial equipment and food supplies into the interior of the USSR: "550 industrial facilities were moved into the interior of the USSR (190 of all-Union and 360 of republican subordination)"; "From the Right Bank to the left bank of the Dnipro were ferried 4,498 tractors, 680 combines, 690 motor vehicles"[4]. February 2022 C0103 Full-Scale Invasion (from February 24, 2022) G0011 Russian Federation S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The large-scale plunder of the economic resources of the occupied territories: "from 2022 to 2025, almost 15 million tonnes of Ukrainian grain, valued at 6.8 billion US dollars, were illegally removed from the temporarily occupied districts of Ukraine"[16]. Strikes on port infrastructure were accompanied by "the destruction of grain and other products destined for export"[17]. The plunder extended to industry: "the owners of the stolen metal - the Azovstal, MMKI and Zaporizhstal plants - have already filed a series of criminal complaints"[18]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Кушева.
