title: Creation of Economic Hopelessness, technique T0141
content: Creation of Economic Hopelessness Aggressors may deliberately create and maintain unbearable socio-economic conditions (acute land shortage, crushing obligations, destitution) in the historical territories of an Indigenous people. This is done to force the population to flee physical and social ruin. As a result, the people 'voluntarily-compulsorily' join the colonizer's militarized structures (for example, the Cossack host or the regular army) or migrate en masse to dangerous imperial frontiers to settle them. This technique allows the empire to accomplish its military and colonization objectives by proxy, disguising state coercion as the victims' own 'free economic choice.' ID: T0141 ⓘ Tactics: Defense Impairment, Extraction of Benefits, Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1847 C1166 "Death sentence" for Lesser Chechnya: the massacre of Duba's hamlet, forest clearings, fortresses, annihilation of the population and stanitsas on the sites of burned auls (1847-1851) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The squeezing of the Chechens out of the mountains was built on depriving them of the means of life - and the empire wrote about this openly. Vorontsov, viceroy and commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, reported to Minister of War Chernyshev in an official letter (otnosheniye) of 25 October 1847: "constrained in their means of life, seeing their constant failures, the Chechens waver, and a large number of families are already resettling into our bounds"[1]. General Sleptsov, in a report of 4 October 1850, built on this a calculation for the future: the mountain communities, "constrained by our future settlements in the valley, ... will inevitably follow the example of their compatriots" - that is, they too would come down to the fortifications[2]. January 1852 C1167 "Neither plow nor sow": the pogrom of Chechnya, organized famine, the buying-up of elites and the institutions of subjugation (1852-1857) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The empire starved the inhabitants of the Khankala gorge out by an openly formulated plan. Imperial historian Volkonsky recorded the design of the summer of 1852: Baryatinsky, who commanded the left flank of the Caucasus Line (the chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), "resolved... to smoke the inhabitants out of the gorge, precisely - to smoke them out, because it was necessary to annihilate with fire everything that gave them subsistence"; the calculation Volkonsky recorded thus - "And to seek food from us means to humble oneself, submit, and willy-nilly resettle"[3]. The same calculation stood behind the razing of Khan-Kala - the inhabitants were to be torn away from Imam Shamil, leader of the highlanders' resistance of Dagestan and Chechnya to the Russian conquest: "the inhabitants, deprived of shelter and sustenance, instead of running over to Shamil, would seek refuge with us"[3]. During the siege of Khan-Kala the detachment cut the aul off from water as well: "the enemy was deprived of the possibility of covered access to the river, and he was left without water"[3]. January 1858 C1022 Muhajirism: the expulsion of Chechens to the Ottoman Empire, the ban on return, and population replacement (1858-1872) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "The principal means of driving out the highlanders became depriving them of their main source of existence – the land. The transfer of vast lands on the plains to Cossack stanitsas left thousands of highlanders without means of subsistence"[4]. Imperial statistics recorded the result: "each family in the auls has 0.5 – 10 desiatinas... With such crowding not only the development of farms, but even the existence of the people cannot be considered secured" (a desiatina is slightly more than a hectare)[5]. Meanwhile the operation's own executors were reporting the opposite. The head of the Argun okrug, Major A. Ippolitov, wrote to the head of the Terek oblast, General Loris-Melikov: "I can positively tell Your Excellency that the people are not even thinking of voluntary resettlement to Turkey; at a general assembly they declared to me that they would go only when the whole of Chechnya leaves to the last man, or when they are ordered to go"[6]. Colonel Bellik on 25 March 1865 reported to the same Loris-Melikov the words of a Chechen: "we will not go to Turkey and will not let those go who are preparing to; in Turkey death awaits us, and it awaits us here too, but here it is more pleasant, because here is our homeland and here lie our fathers, slain by the Russians"[6]. January 1860 C1171 Land plunder: the colonial repartition of land, land hunger and Cossack colonization of the Terek oblast (1860-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov give a summary based on the materials of the Caucasus Military District (RGVIA, f. 1300, op. 7, d. 3) and the work of A. I. Khasbulatov: "According to the data of 1877, in Mountain Chechnya, including Ichkeria, with a population of almost 100 thousand people, there was on average 0.3 desiatinas (a desiatina is a little over a hectare) of arable land per capita... such fantastic landlessness as in Mountain Chechnya was known to no other region of the Russian Empire"[4]. In 1901 on the Chechen plain "a family (usually quite numerous) had from 7 to 14 desiatinas"[6]. The count by family budget was kept by the oblast statistics service itself: "A Cossack family had a gross income of 918 rubles from its land allotment... and was left with a surplus of 140 rubles. The richest Chechen family on the plain, according to the Terek Oblast Statistical Committee (1903), received an income of 262 rubles from its land allotment while spending 414 rubles on its upkeep; the deficit came to 152 rubles"[6]. January 1906 C0069 Stolypin Repressions and Mass Displacement (1906–1914) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The economic squeezing of peasants onto the imperial frontier under the guise of free choice: "during 1906–12 about 1 million people left Ukraine for Asiatic Russia. The largest number of resettlers came from Left-Bank Ukraine, whose peasantry suffered from land scarcity"[7]; land and credit were unobtainable at home, while "Low land prices beyond the Urals and encouraging government credits… attracted the poor peasantry and prompted it to migrate"[7] – state coercion was disguised as voluntary resettlement. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References В. title: Predatory Raids, technique T0148
content: Predatory Raids Aggressors may organize armed attacks on the settlements of an Indigenous people for the purpose of looting, seizing material valuables, driving off livestock, and taking civilians captive. This practice depletes the demographic and economic potential of the colonized society, deprives people of the resources needed for survival, and creates a zone of constant physical threat around the metropole's installations. title: Deprivation of Electricity and Heating, technique T0124
content: Deprivation of Electricity and Heating Aggressors may systematically destroy energy infrastructure facilities, thermal power plants, and power transmission lines to create conditions incompatible with normal life. Mass deprivation of basic necessities serves as a form of collective punishment aimed at physically and psychologically breaking the society's will to resist. title: Deprivation of Drinking Water, technique T0123
content: Deprivation of Drinking Water Aggressors may deliberately destroy water supply infrastructure (water utilities, pumping stations, dams) or physically block access to natural sources. Disabling this critical life-support system is used to create catastrophic sanitary and epidemiological conditions and to break the population's capacity for defense. ID: T0123 ⓘ Tactic: Defense Impairment Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram

title: Cultural Assimilation, technique T0115
content: Cultural Assimilation Aggressors may apply comprehensive measures to displace and replace the unique cultural codes of the Indigenous people with the standards and traditions of the metropole. The artificial dissolution of the local culture within the aggressor's dominant culture makes it possible to sever historical continuity, deprive the colonized society of its national identity, and ensure its irreversible mental merger with the colonizing state. title: Cultural Assimilation: Replacement of the Native Language's Alphabet, sub-technique T0115.001
content: Cultural Assimilation: Replacement of the Native Language's Alphabet As part of cultural assimilation, aggressors may forcibly change the graphic basis (alphabet) of the local population's language. Converting the script of the Indigenous people to the metropole's alphabet artificially cuts new generations off from the body of previously published national literature, historical documents, and cultural heritage, while simultaneously facilitating linguistic unification and creating the false impression of illiteracy and the absence of a written tradition before the arrival of the colonizers. That is, either the metropole's orthography or an archaic one was admissible - contemporary Ukrainian orthography was not allowed in any form. title: Cultural Assimilation: Cultural Chauvinism, sub-technique T0115.003
content: Cultural Assimilation: Cultural Chauvinism As part of cultural assimilation, aggressors may systematically impose, through state institutions and media, the idea of the unconditional superiority of the metropole's culture over the culture of the colonized society. Cultivating a contemptuous attitude toward the art, traditions, and customs of the local population instills in it an inferiority complex, stimulating mass voluntary renunciation of one's own roots for the sake of successful integration into the aggressor's society. title: Cultural Assimilation: Folklorization of the Native Culture, sub-technique T0115.002
content: Cultural Assimilation: Folklorization of the Native Culture As part of cultural assimilation, aggressors may deliberately reduce the rich and multifaceted culture of the Indigenous people to primitive, entertainment-oriented, or exclusively rural folklore. Pushing local traditions out of the academic, philosophical, and urban spheres into the category of archaic ethnography allows the colonizer to artificially secure for its own culture the status of the sole bearer of progress and civilization. ID: T0115.002 ⓘ Tactic: Persistence Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram

title: Theft of Cultural Property, technique T0112
content: Theft of Cultural Property Aggressors may carry out the systematic looting, unlawful confiscation, and removal of historical artifacts, works of art, archives, and relics from seized territories. This technique is used for the direct extraction of benefits by enriching the metropole's collections while simultaneously depriving the colonized society of its material historical foundation. title: Use as a Buffer Zone, technique T0067
content: Use as a Buffer Zone Aggressors may deliberately use captured territories as a buffer between themselves and external threats. This technique serves the extraction of benefits by ensuring the long-term military and geopolitical security of the colonizer. Such a practice makes it possible to create a protective gray zone that absorbs external strikes and shifts the costs of any conflicts exclusively onto the colonized peoples, while shielding the aggressor's central regions. ID: T0067 ⓘ Tactic: Extraction of Benefits Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram

title: Creation of Hazardous Industries, technique T0051
content: Creation of Hazardous Industries Aggressors may site environmentally harmful enterprises, raw-material extraction facilities producing toxic waste, or landfills for the disposal of hazardous materials on seized territories. Shifting destructive industrial burdens onto the lands of the Indigenous people allows the colonizer to enrich the metropole and safeguard its own environment while cynically ignoring the catastrophic consequences for the health of the local population and the environment of the colonized region. ID: T0051 ⓘ Tactic: Extraction of Benefits Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram

title: Taxation, technique T0056
content: Taxation Aggressors may establish direct control over the fiscal system in seized territories, redirecting levies collected from the local population straight into their own treasury. Introducing new taxes, shifting the financial burden of imperial wars onto the shoulders of an Indigenous people, and artificially lowering the social status of local residents in order to subject them to maximum economic taxation allow the colonizer to systematically siphon off resources and exhaust the region's economy. ID: T0056 ⓘ Tactic: Extraction of Benefits ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1614 C1114 Deprivation of the Nokhchi of political agency and the imposition of alien governance (1614–1616) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration imposed tribute on the highland Nokhchi societies: an extract from the book of the Terek town's Prikaz office records that the administration sent people «to the Michkizes for the sovereign's yasak»[1]. January 1617 C1115 Economic Exploitation and Creation of Dependency of the Nokhchi (1617–1622) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration used the physical loss of documents to artificially lower the social status of local residents for the purpose of taxing them economically: an extract of the Posolsky Prikaz concerning a petition to Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich states that after «the sovereign's charter of grant was lost», the heirs of the deceased Nokhchi delegate were stripped of their privileges and «made equal in everything with the Okochans, with the plowing people, and carts and wagons are exacted from them», whereas previously «no taxes whatsoever had been taken» from them[1]. January 1626 C1116 Use of the Nokhchi in Military Expeditions, Intervention, and Imposition of Yasak (1626–1628) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration imposed an annual tribute in kind on the Nokhchi mountain communities (the Shibutians): a report from the Terek voivodes Ivan Andreyevich Dashkov and Bogdan Gerasimovich Priklonsky to the Posolsky Prikaz states that when subjecthood was formalized in 1627, the mountaineers were required «to give yasak at one kul (sack) of honey per year»[1]. September 1665 C0024 The Moscow Articles of Ivan Briukhovetsky (1665) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government Direct extraction of the autonomy's economic resources: "The collection of taxes from the Ukrainian population (except for the Cossack estate) was entrusted to the tsarist administration. The collected funds were channeled into the tsar's treasury"[2]. January 1667 C0005 Truce of Andrusovo (1667) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government Having gained political power over the Left Bank, Moscow immediately attempted to seize the right to collect taxes in order to extract resources directly: "the attempts of Russian voivodes... to introduce their own taxation system in Ukraine led only to revolts (for example... the attempted census of 1666...)"[3]. January 1691 C1124 Punitive Raids and the Economic Strangulation of the Nokhchi (1691–1700) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration of the Tsardom of Muscovy imposed discriminatory levies on Nokhchi societies for the internal movement of goods: the historian Sh. B. Akhmadov emphasizes that «the Okochans (Akkin Chechens) living in the town of Terki were obliged without exception to pay duty on the various goods and wares they took out for sale to their compatriots in Chechnya and Ingushetia»[4]. January 1695 C0010 Azov Campaigns and Fortress Construction (1695–1700) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government Shifting the financial and logistical burden of imperial wars onto the autonomy's shoulders: "The commoners supplied provisions for the volunteer troops, and they also stocked hay for the winter for the host's artillery"[3][5]. January 1726 C1131 Economic Discrimination and Reconnaissance of Territories (1726–1728) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration of the Russian Empire levied discriminatory duties on the movement of goods of the Indigenous population: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov quotes the customs books, stating that in 1726 "on the travel document of the Terek resident, the Okochanin Kurman Bogomatov... duties of 24 altyns in money were collected by decree"[6]. January 1765 C0031 Abolition of the Cossack Order in Sloboda Ukraine (1765) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government Lowering the social status of the indigenous population for the purpose of economic extraction: "The Cossacks and their helpers were turned into military settlers and taxed with the poll tax," and those with the right to distill horilka "now had to pay… 95 kopecks per soul to the treasury"[7]. August 1832 C1155 Extermination of 61 settlements of lowland Chechnya and mountainous Ichkeria by Rosen's troops, burning alive of the defenders of Germenchuk, and extortion of hostages from 80 villages (1832) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army In September 1832, corps commander Rosen imposed on the villages of Chechnya and Ichkeria an annual tribute from each household as a condition of being spared. The imperial historian Volkonsky wrote: "from the village of Metso-erzo-yurt, amanats (hostages) were taken along with a tribute of one ruble per hearth"; the villages of Eshta-kale and Eyni-kale undertook "to pay henceforth a tribute of 1 ruble per hearth"[8]. Rosen reported to Minister of War Chernyshev: the village of Gurdali "handed over an amanat and undertook to pay tribute"[9]. The tribute was exacted from a people whose villages and crops were in those very days being exterminated by the troops. August 1836 C1157 Coercion of Devastated Zandak into Subordination and Tribute by Colonel Pullo (1836) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army On 27 August 1836, Colonel Pullo imposed tribute on the aul of Zandak on the Yaman-su river, devastated by his detachment on 23 August 1836 (campaign C1156): payment of tribute became a condition for accepting the crushed village's "submission". In a report to General Petrov dated 27 August 1836, Pullo recorded the obligation accepted by the elders at the Groznaya fortress: "to pay, on a par with the Aukhovites and other submissive tribes, the established tribute"[10]. The tribute was not the village's counter-offer but the empire's standing norm for taxing the societies it deemed "submissive"; refusal would have meant the return of the "avenging arms of the Russians" - the village had just survived devastation, the captivity of its inhabitants, and the seizure of its livestock[10]. September 1836 C1163 The amanat-and-tribute system of colonel Pullo in the seized auls of Chechnya (1836-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The amanat-and-tribute system of Pullo, commander of the left flank of the Caucasus Line (a chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), imposed a tribute on the seized auls of Chechnya. Pullo in a memorandum of 1840: "As the highland communities were subjugated, each handed over amanats, paid a tribute of one silver ruble per saklia, handed over all Russian captives held by it" (saklia - a highlander's house: the tribute was levied on every house; amanats - hostages whom the empire took away from the auls to control them)[10]. The 1840 register of the highland peoples, published in the documentary collection «Движение горцев северо-восточного Кавказа в 20-50 гг. XIX века» together with Pullo's memorandum, calls the tribute a punishment outright: the Qachqalyq people, the Michik Chechens and the Aukhovites (Chechen communities of eastern Chechnya) "pay a tribute imposed on them as punishment for repeated revolts", and the Chechens living beyond the Sunzha river, "as punishment for revolt, have been burdened with a tribute"[10]. The money was squeezed out regularly: general Grabbe, commander of the troops of the Caucasus Line and Pullo's superior, in a report to the empire's Minister of War Chernyshev of 23 March 1840, named the regular payment of tributes a sign of the "tranquility" that had set in - the report lists the "regular payment of tributes and duties" weeks before the uprising[11]. Muhammad Tahir al-Qarakhi, the chronicler of Shamil (Shamil - imam, leader of the resistance of the highlanders of Dagestan and Chechnya to the Russian conquest), named this exaction - one ruble from every house and one gun from every ten houses - as the reason the Chechens called upon Shamil. November 1838 C1164 Forcing Chechnya into submission after the fall of Akhulgo and suppression of the general uprising of 1840 (1838-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The winter expeditions of general Pullo, who commanded the left flank of the Caucasus Line (the chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), collected money from the Chechen auls under the name of tribute. The imperial historian Yurov tallied the December 1839 march: "In all, during this bloodless military promenade, 3779 rubles and 455 rifles were collected, and 97 abreks, 7 captives and two fugitives were handed over" (abrek - the empire's label for an outlawed highlander)[12], and the January 1840 march along the Michik river: the auls "obediently presented 2463 rubles, 545 rifles, cattle for the detachment's provisioning, and handed over 30 abreks"[12]. After the suppression of the uprising the levy was fixed as a fine: point 10 of the "Conditions prescribed to submitting highlanders", issued by general Grabbe, commander of the troops of the Caucasus Line, on 15 June 1840, prescribed "As punishment for participation in Shamil's uprising, to pay a fine of two rams from every saklia" (saklia - a highlander's house; Shamil - the imam, leader of the resistance of the highlanders of Dagestan and Chechnya to the Russian conquest)[10]. April 1858 C1170 "Military-Popular Administration": the Colonial Regime of the Terek Oblast (1858-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations Historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova writes: from the 1860s the administrative apparatus in Chechnya and Ingushetia "was maintained chiefly on funds collected from the people"[13]. The empire did not trust the highlanders with military service - and taxed them in money instead: by the laws of 2 and 9 June 1887 a monetary levy in place of military service was introduced for the Muslims of the Terek oblast, its size "did not exceed 22 kopecks per 'dym'"[13] ("dym" - a separate household, homestead)[13]; historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov confirm: "in 1887 the Russian government introduced a special monetary levy for them"[14]. From then on the levies only grew: "From 1887 to 1905 the sum of taxes rose from 228.1 to 678.8 thousand rubles, that is, it nearly tripled over these years", while the podymnaya tax - the tax on each household - "in the Terek oblast reached in the 1890s up to 70 kopecks per desiatina, while at that time in the interior provinces of the country it was no more than 17 kopecks, or four times less"[13]. On top of the levy, village communities bore obligations in kind: maintaining the elder and the village board, the roads, ditches and watch posts[14]. August 1914 C1189 First World War in Chechnya: removal of the "unreliable element" into the "Savage Division", extraordinary security and mobilization of strikers (1914-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations From the formation of the Chechen regiment in 1914 the Russian Empire laid its upkeep on the Chechen communities themselves: the full equipment of each horseman cost 300 rubles, and it was paid not by the treasury but by the village communities that had recommended the man into the regiment. Historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov write: "the upkeep of the national regiments lay as a heavy burden on the peasant-highlanders"[14]. State funds did not suffice for the rest either: the new horses assembled to replenish the division in the autumn of 1916 were, as the same historians write, "very poor", and the division's command sought the allocation of funds to buy horses[14]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Кушева. title: Aggressor Claiming Victim Status, technique T0005
content: Aggressor Claiming Victim Status Aggressors may use propaganda instruments to invert roles, presenting their own offensive actions as a forced measure of self-defense. By claiming fictitious threats from the local population or external forces, the aggressor constructs a false narrative in which it acts solely as a defender of its own interests or security. This makes it possible to morally justify the invasion and shift the blame for the escalation of violence onto the colonized society. ID: T0005 ⓘ Tactic: Legitimization of Domination ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1800 C1106 Propagandistic Inversion of Roles and Dehumanization (1800–1864) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration of the Russian Empire stripped the Indigenous population of the status of a legitimate adversary by applying an inversion of meanings: historian Ya. Z. Akhmadov states that lawful defense was labeled with criminal terms, and «The anti-colonial and anti-feudal uprisings of the population of Chechnya, referred to in official documents as 'mischief', 'robberies', and 'murders', were perceived by the Russian autocracy as a challenge and an insult»[1], which served as a formal pretext for punitive actions. January 1809 C1141 Consolidation in Chechnya: Bribery of Elders, Economic Control, and Setting Neighbors against One Another (1809-1811) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The Russian Empire shifted the blame for the devastation it had wrought onto the victimized people itself. In a proclamation to the inhabitants of the Chechen land, the commander-in-chief in the Caucasus, General Tormasov, presented the pogrom of 1807 as a consequence of the inhabitants' own actions: «the raids and depredations that you carried out within the borders of Russia brought upon you righteous wrath… you yourselves were the cause of the misfortune that befell you three years ago» — and threatened a new invasion, «to bring sword and flame upon the guilty», offering «mercy» in exchange for submission[2]. April 2014 C0101 Continuation of the Russo-Ukrainian War: Armed Aggression in the Donbas (2014–2015) G0011 Russian Federation S0021 Propaganda The exploitation of the Odesa tragedy to build a state propaganda myth and invert the roles: the actual picture, per the UN, is clashes "between supporters of unity and supporters of the federalization of Ukraine, as a result of which 48 people died," while the investigation remains incomplete and "no one has yet been held to account"[3]. The tragedy was used as moral justification for further aggression - by the same device as the "crucified boy" fake, for which "there is no evidence to support Pyshniak's claim"[4]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Ахмадов Я. title: Labor Exploitation, technique T0057
content: Labor Exploitation Aggressors may forcibly conscript the local population into heavy, dangerous, or unpaid labor in the interests of the metropole. This technique serves the direct extraction of benefits through the use of free or extremely cheap labor for the implementation of the colonizer's state megaprojects and military or industrial needs. At the same time, this practice is used for the neutralization of defenses: the removal of the able-bodied population from the region's economy and labor under conditions associated with high mortality physically exhaust the society and reduce its demographic potential. ID: T0057 ⓘ Tactics: Extraction of Benefits, Defense Impairment ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1614 C1114 Deprivation of the Nokhchi of political agency and the imposition of alien governance (1614–1616) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The appointed administration forced the Indigenous population into unpaid labor: historian E. N. Kusheva points out that the Kabardian prince Sunchaley Yanglychevich Cherkassky compelled the service Okochans of the Terek town subordinate to him «to make all manner of wares for him, to plow the fields and to mow the hay»[1]. The metropole itself went years without paying for the military service of the Indigenous population: a report from the Terek voivode Pyotr Petrovich Golovin to the Astrakhan voivode Ivan Nikitich Odoyevsky records that they «serve the sovereign tsar... in all manner of the sovereign's Terek... services... yet have not been granted the sovereign's monetary and grain salary for the tenth year now»[2]. January 1617 C1115 Economic Exploitation and Creation of Dependency of the Nokhchi (1617–1622) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The occupation administration deliberately exhausted the Indigenous population materially, forcing them to perform compulsory service at their own expense: in a petition submitted to Tsar Mikhail Fyodorovich, the Okotsky murza Kokhostrov Biytemirov and the serving Okochans of Tersky Town reported that, because their allowance went unpaid, they «were left without grain, have utterly perished from hunger and every hardship, have fallen, sovereign, into great debt, and are dying a death of starvation together with our wives and little children»[3]. January 1695 C0010 Azov Campaigns and Fortress Construction (1695–1700) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army The forced use of Cossacks to build imperial infrastructure under harsh conditions: "in the making of fortifications around the Kyiv-Pechersk Monastery"[4][5]. January 1700 C0011 Integration Reforms of Peter I and the Great Northern War (1700–1708) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army The mass conscription of the population for the construction of military installations in Moscow's interests. The tsar officially thanked the hetman and the starshyna for their "diligent zeal (and considerable labors borne) in the making of the Pechersk fortification" and promised for this "service and labors in the making of the said fortification" his "most exalted favor"[4]. January 1704 C0017 Forced Labor on Imperial Construction: The Ladoga Canal (1704–1725) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0010 Regular Army The mass mobilization of Cossack regiments for penal construction labor: the digging of the Ladoga Canal "was carried out chiefly by the hands of Ukrainian Cossacks," and there "tens of thousands of people perished from back-breaking labor, hunger and the harsh climate"[6]. In 1721 a "10,000-strong Cossack corps" headed by P. Polubotok was dispatched to the canal[7]; the works continued through 1721–23[8]. January 1817 C0041 Introduction of Military Settlements and Liquidation of the Danubian Sich (1817–1828) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The transfer of Cossacks to the status of rightless military settlers (the Arakcheev system), which provoked the uprising of 1817: "The trigger was the order abolishing the Buh Cossack Host and turning the Cossacks into military settlers… The reprisal against the rebellious Cossacks was extraordinarily brutal: many were cut down with sabers, drowned in the Southern Buh, flogged to death"[9]. There were two acts, on opposite sides of the uprising: the nominal decree of April 17, 1817 transferred the Buh Host's district "into direct military administration" (PSZRI, vol. XXXIV, no. 26,802) - this was the trigger; the decree of October 8, 1817 (no. 27,081), issued after the suppression, formalized the liquidation: "the name of the Buh Cossack Host is abolished"[10]. January 1817 C1021 Destruction of the Nokhchi Villages along the Sunzha and Erection of the Groznaya Fortress in Their Place (1817–1818) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The Regular Army of the Russian Empire forced Chechen villages to make deliveries and perform labor for the construction of the fortress. Imperial general Yermolov testifies in his "Notes": "the villages from which we held amanats were ordered to deliver timber for the construction"; the nearest villages "dared not show disobedience"[11]. March 1820 C1145 Night Attack on the Aul of Topli, Burning of Germenchuk, and Coercion of the Nokhchi to Fell Their Own Forests (1820) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The Russian Empire forcibly compelled the Nokhchi to work for the conqueror — to cut clearings through their own forests. The imperial historian Potto writes that Grekov, commander of the left flank, "gathered the elders of the surrounding villages and ordered them to send out workers with axes for the felling at once," and under threat of reprisal "compelled the Chechens to obey," after which the conscripted inhabitants cut a clearing through their own forest[12]. March 1821 C1146 Suppression of the Nokhchi Uprising: Devastation of Villages and Forced Forest Felling by Grekov (1821-1822) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The Russian Empire compelled the Nokhchi themselves to cut military clearings through their own forests. Historian D. A. Khozhaev writes that in imposing the line, the conquerors "compelled the subordinated Highlanders to heavy labor building roads and bridges," while those who evaded it were "fined mercilessly, with their livestock and property confiscated"[13]. The imperial historian Potto confirms that the clearings from Amir-Adzhi-Yurt to Oisungur, Isti-Su, and Gerzel-Aul "through the narrow forested strip… were worked by the natives themselves, under the supervision of the Aksai princes"[12]. September 1836 C1163 The amanat-and-tribute system of colonel Pullo in the seized auls of Chechnya (1836-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The amanat-and-tribute system of Pullo, commander of the left flank of the Caucasus Line (a chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), included forced labor: the troops forced the inhabitants of the seized auls of Chechnya to fell their own forest by allotment. The imperial historian Yurov recorded of the December 1839 expedition that under the pressure of the detachment the inhabitants of the auls "felled forest by allotment at Gekhi, at the Valerik tract and between the villages of Shali and Malaya Ataga" (Gekhi, Valerik, Shali, Malaya Ataga - Chechen villages and tracts; "by allotment" - by a forced apportionment imposed by the troops alongside the tribute and the surrender of weapons)[14]. The forest the inhabitants were made to fell was the environment of life and the shelter of the Chechen communities. February 1837 C1161 Coercion of Chechnya into Oaths by Feze's Spring Tour: Amanats from Communities Coerced into the Oath, Destruction of Auls along the Dzhalka, a Livestock Fine (February-April 1837) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The submission taken by Feze's troops in February 1837 immediately turned into labor duty. Rozen's report to Minister of War Chernyshev of 4 March 1837 records: on 21 February "the inhabitants of six neighboring auls declared their submission and sent out workers to cut, together with the Kumyks, a road in the forests through the Qachqalyq mountains along the Michik"[15] - communities just subordinated were set by the empire to cut the forest for a military road against themselves; the duty came as part of the package of submission, as the standard "Conditions Prescribed to Submitting Highlanders" would later codify it. November 1838 C1164 Forcing Chechnya into submission after the fall of Akhulgo and suppression of the general uprising of 1840 (1838-1840) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The "Conditions prescribed to submitting highlanders", issued by general Grabbe, commander of the troops of the Caucasus Line (the chain of imperial fortifications on the land of the Nokhchi), on 15 June 1840, imposed labour duty on the Chechen auls. Point 4 prescribed: "in case of a detachment's movement to allot people for building roads and bridges, to keep at the pristav's disposal a sufficient number of people for carrying papers or orders from one aul to another, to give mounted men for escort duty" (pristav - a superintendent over the auls appointed by the empire)[16]. April 1877 C1172 "Mow Down Everything, Beat and Hang Without Mercy": Suppression of the 1877 Uprising and the Executions in Grozny (1877-1878) G0009 Russian Empire S0010 Regular Army The order of Colonel Lokhvitsky of 17 July 1877 for the Cheberloy uchastok obliged the punished themselves to cut a road for the troops into their own mountains: "the entire uchastok is to be obliged right now, within the very shortest time, to make a wide forest clearing (proseka) from the Bosoevskaya mountain to the Sharo-Argun river over a stretch of upwards of 6 versts" (a verst is slightly over a kilometer)[17]. January 1890 C0066 Industrial Colonization and Resource Exploitation of the South (1890) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The use of cheap labor at the mines and plants under conditions of harsh exploitation: "Initially the majority of miners were seasonal workers"[18] – without rights, without settlement, worked to exhaustion. January 1928 C0077 Forced Collectivization and Dekulakization (1928–1932) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services Use of dekulakized peasants, sent into the emerging GULAG system, as forced unpaid labor for heavy state projects[19]. August 1932 C0078 Terror by Famine: The Holodomor (1932–1933) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services Lethally dangerous exploitation of the labor of Ukrainian peasants, convicted en masse under the "law of five ears of grain" and exiled to corrective labor camps during the Holodomor[19]. September 1939 C0081 Annexation and Sovietization of Western Ukraine (1939–1941) G0010 USSR S0017 Secret Police and Security Services The transfer of hundreds of thousands of people into special settlements and camps as a system of forced labor: in under two years "up to 1,250,000 people (about 10% of the population) were removed to remote regions of the USSR"[20] – the deportees were assigned to labor in remote regions with no right to leave. title: Sale of Territory, technique T0066
content: Sale of Territory Aggressors may conduct commercial transactions transferring seized lands, together with the Indigenous people living on them, to the control of third states in exchange for financial compensation. In carrying out such a diplomatic-economic operation, the colonizer treats the territory purely as a liquid asset for replenishing its own treasury, while the sovereignty, rights, and national interests of the local society are completely and demonstratively ignored. ID: T0066 ⓘ Tactic: Extraction of Benefits Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram

title: Forced Passportization, technique T0035
content: Forced Passportization Aggressors may mass-impose their citizenship and issue the metropole's state-standard documents to residents of occupied territories. Coercing the Indigenous people into obtaining new passports under threat of losing basic rights, medical care, or property allows the colonizer to artificially integrate the population into its legal framework, convert them into the status of its own subjects, and justify the continued retention of the region as the "protection of its citizens." ID: T0035 ⓘ Tactic: Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: April 1858 C1170 "Military-Popular Administration": the Colonial Regime of the Terek Oblast (1858-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The 1894 "Regulation on Residence Permits" enshrined estate inequality: nobles, officials and merchants received passport books of unlimited duration, while highlanders ascribed to village communities received five-year books or short-term passports and bilets (written passes) for absence[1]. Historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova states the regime's effect from the oblast's records: "Terek highlanders, should they appear beyond the Kuban or in other parts of the Russian Empire without passports, were considered vagrants and malefactors and were punished as such"; she also writes: "The passport system served the administration of the Terek oblast as a favourite means of constraining even persons well known to it"[1]. Inside the oblast a regime of absences operated: leave of up to a month was granted by the village elder, for a longer term - by the okrug head; unauthorized absence was punished by fine, arrest or public works, and a highlander could not move from one community to another without the consent of two village communities - the one he was leaving and the one he was joining[2]. February 2022 C0103 Full-Scale Invasion (from February 24, 2022) G0011 Russian Federation S0024 Police Apparatus Coercing residents of the occupied territories into taking Russian passports: "the policy of mass conferral of Russian citizenship to residents of occupied areas of Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions exacerbated the coercive environment there," and "those who refused Russian passports were denied access to public services, notably social security, healthcare, and education, and risked unemployment" and "faced a heightened risk of arbitrary detention when crossing checkpoints"[3]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Ибрагимова З. title: Legal Segregation of the Population, technique T0032
content: Legal Segregation of the Population Aggressors may introduce discriminatory norms at the legislative level that restrict the basic rights of the Indigenous people compared with representatives of the metropole. This technique is used for the institutional consolidation of control. Creating artificial barriers in access to education, government positions, property ownership, or freedom of movement (including the creation of zones of artificial settlement) allows the colonizer to marginalize the local population and fix its subordinate status in the social hierarchy being constructed. ID: T0032 ⓘ Tactic: Persistence ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1781 C0034 Administrative Dismantling and Enserfment of the Left Bank (1781–1786) G0009 Russian Empire S0024 Police Apparatus The legal enserfment of Ukrainian peasants by Catherine II's decree of May 3, 1783, depriving them of the right of free movement: "For the certain and reliable collection of treasury revenues in the viceroyalties of Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Novhorod-Siverskyi and for the prevention of any flights… each of the villagers is to remain in the place and station where he is registered by the current last revision"[1]. January 1791 C0036 Establishment of the "Pale of Settlement" (1791) G0009 Russian Empire S0024 Police Apparatus The introduction of territorial discrimination: by the decree of 1791, the Jewish population's right to burgher and merchant status was confined to specific viceroyalties – Ekaterinoslav and Taurida[2] – the legal foundation of the future Pale of Settlement, which confined the area of residence and economic activity to the colonized governorates. February 1845 C1173 Colonial oil: the seizure of the Grozny subsoil and the rent of the Cossack host (1845-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations By orders for the Terek oblast of 15 August 1890 and March 1897 the Russian Empire forbade the Chechen village communities "to enter into any agreements with mining industrialists" without the government's permission - "The guilty, in the person of village officials, were brought to account, and suits were brought in the courts to annul the concluded contracts"[3]. The ground of the ban is formulated by historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova: "The aul communities were deprived of the right to lease out oil-bearing plots - the land was granted to them not by right of property but only into use with the right of surface working; its subsoil was considered the property of the treasury"[3]. When the Ministry of Agriculture confirmed rules that allowed peasant communities to lease out their own land for the working of the subsoil, the head of the Terek oblast, General Kakhanov, in 1894 "categorically objected to the extension to the Chechen lands" of these rules - and demanded that, even if the communities' rights were recognized, the resolution on leasing the land be confirmed by the uchastok chief and a third of the income go "to pay the podymnaya tax of the communities concerned"[4]. For the Cossacks the opposite rule was in force: from 1891, when subsoil passed to the treasury, stanitsas were entitled to replacement land or compensation - "For the Chechen communities no reserve land allotments were provided by the state. Still less was there any question of material reward"[3]. April 1858 C1170 "Military-Popular Administration": the Colonial Regime of the Terek Oblast (1858-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations From 1882 "especially important" cases in which the accused were highlanders were transferred to the field court-martial; in 1893, with the emperor's permission, a significant share of highlanders' criminal cases was withdrawn from the general civil courts - into whose jurisdiction these cases passed, the source does not specify[5]. Punishment could also be imposed without any court: the head of the oblast jailed highlanders for up to one month at his personal discretion, and imposed penalties on aul communities for harbouring[5]; on 19 November 1893 the rules of administrative deportation to Eastern Siberia on accusation or suspicion of stealing horses and livestock were extended to the Terek oblast[5], and according to historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov the decision on administrative exile for a term of up to five years was taken by the commander of the Caucasus Army, and the place of exile was Chechen Island in the Caspian[4]. The 1894 "Temporary Regulation on Measures to Restrain the Native Population of the Terek Oblast from 'Predation'" - its draft was submitted for approval by the head of the Terek oblast, general Kakhanov - according to historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova, wrote the collective liability of the village community for committed crimes into law[5]; historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov record the mechanics: mountain villages paid for stolen livestock "if the tracks of the stolen livestock turned out to be lost near the given village", while "the possibility that the thieves might not be highlanders at all was completely ignored"[4]. Indigenous inhabitants were barred from holding the posts of pristav and okrug head and from serving as justices of the peace[5]; the 1888 regulation on the administration of the Terek and Kuban oblasts established, in the words of historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova, "a narrowly caste-based military-Cossack administration, without the participation not only of representatives of the mountain peoples but of the non-Cossack element as well... the highlanders were placed outside the operation of the general laws"[5]. In the 1890s the administration, by a separate order, forbade Cossacks to keep kunachestvo with highlanders (kunachestvo - sworn brotherhood, an institution of friendship between households)[5]. Service was segregated too: the "political unreliability" of the Caucasus Muslims led the authorities to give up forming line units from them, and from 1886, by order of the Minister of War, recruits from the Terek oblast were assigned only to troops stationed in the Caucasus[5]. Zemstvos were never introduced in the oblast at all; the proposal on zemstvo institutions in the Terek oblast, submitted to the State Duma in 1914, was not adopted before the revolution[5]. January 1860 C1171 Land plunder: the colonial repartition of land, land hunger and Cossack colonization of the Terek oblast (1860-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations The allotment norm was written out by estate and origin: "Cossacks are allotted 30 desiatinas (a desiatina is a little over a hectare) per soul, while natives get no more than 2-5 desiatinas"[3]; the gap was also entrenched by the general rules of allotment: by the count of the newspaper Kazachy Vestnik for 1884, on which historian Z. Kh. Ibragimova relies, Russian residents of the Caucasus krai received "24–30 desiatinas of land allotment per soul, whereas natives got 12–18 desiatinas per dym, which on average numbered 5 men" (a dym is a hearth, a household)[3]. In 1886 in the Grozny okrug "an average Chechen family with many children... had 11 desiatinas of land, while the average Cossack family owned more than 92 desiatinas"[4]. By Order No. 418 of the viceroy of 1863, "the right to buy land plots from the local population was received by Russian officers and officials of the oblast administration"[3] - an ordinary Chechen could not be a buyer of that same category of land; the rules of 1 March 1902 instituted the buying-up of privately owned lands "for the needs of the Caucasus Cossack hosts, at the expense of their capital funds"[3]. October 1905 C1175 Collective punishment in the abrek era: fines, quartering of troops and exile for Zelimkhan (1905-1913) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations On 24 October 1905 the Russian Empire imposed martial law "in the Grozny, Vedeno and Khasav-Yurt okrugs of the Terek oblast, that is, in the whole of Chechnya", and on 23 December extended it to the entire oblast[4]. The weapons ban "applied exclusively to the highlanders and the out-of-town settlers and did not extend to the Cossacks. Moreover... the Viceroy of the Caucasus ordered that 10 thousand single-shot Berdan rifles and a million cartridges be distributed to the Cossacks of the Terek oblast free of charge"[4]. On 22 June 1909 martial law was lifted - but "in the Terek oblast a 'state of reinforced protection' was introduced at the same time", whose ordinances "effectively reduced to 'nought' the democratic rights and freedoms 'granted' by the imperial decree of 17 October 1905"[4]. January 1906 C0050 Destruction of Ukrainian Societies and Segregation (1906–1910) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The official classing of the indigenous population as aliens: Stolypin prescribed to the governors to refuse the registration of "any alien societies whatsoever, including Ukrainian and Jewish ones, regardless of the aims they pursue"[6]. August 1914 C1189 First World War in Chechnya: removal of the "unreliable element" into the "Savage Division", extraordinary security and mobilization of strikers (1914-1917) G0009 Russian Empire S0012 Occupation and Controlled Administrations On 13 August 1914 the Russian Empire placed the Terek oblast under the regime of "extraordinary security" - an imperial regime that handed the residents over to the extrajudicial powers of the administration - and then the oblast administration issued an order "on the protection of tranquility at the enterprises", under which the fate of "violators of tranquility" was decided by military courts[4]. How this worked can be seen from the strike of May 1916 at the Grozny oil fields: the administration brought armed Cossacks onto the fields, they arrested 13 workers, and, as historians Ya. Z. Akhmadov and E. Kh. Khasmagomadov remark, "all those arrested turned out to be Muslims"[4]. The police arrested nine more workers on the first day of the strike - for sounding the alarm whistles of the plants[4]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Екатерина II (ПСЗРИ, т. title: Rewriting of History, technique T0004
content: Rewriting of History Aggressors may initiate the creation and mass dissemination of artificial historical concepts designed to substantiate their claim to foreign territories. Constructing a new historical canon, in which facts are distorted and the chronology of events is tailored to the interests of the metropole, allows the aggressor to retroactively legalize the occupation, convincing both its own population and the local one of the historical inevitability and legality of the absorption. ID: T0004 ⓘ Tactic: Legitimization of Domination ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1550 C1104 Religious Frontier and the Fabrication of Historical Right (1550–1721) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0008 Government The government of the Tsardom of Muscovy fabricated historical narratives to provide legal justification for the invasion of new territories: historian Michael Khodarkovsky points out that in diplomatic correspondence officials deliberately constructed fictitious claims that the Indigenous peoples of the Caucasus had allegedly, since ancient times, been Muscovite "subjects in the Riazan region, who then fled from Riazan and settled in the mountains"[1]. January 1674 C0006 Publication of the "Synopsis" (1674) G0008 Tsardom of Muscovy S0011 Moscow Patriarchate For the ideological justification of the seizure, the Muscovite authorities received a ready-made historical canon: "the 'SYNOPSIS,' 'Synopsis, or a Brief Collection from Various Chroniclers on the Origin of the Slaveno-Rossian People' – a historical work first published by the printing house of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra (1674)"[2] – the book constructed a shared "Slaveno-Rossian" past, legitimizing Moscow's rule over Kyiv retroactively. January 1721 C1108 Imposition of an Image of Backwardness and the “Civilizing” Mission (1721–1800s) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The government of the Russian Empire fabricated historical accounts to provide legal justification for invasion: historian Michael Khodarkovsky points out that in 1748 and in the 1770s officials deliberately constructed fictitious claims that the Indigenous peoples of the Caucasus had allegedly been Christians in the past, in order to contest the claims of other empires and "legitimize their efforts at their 're-Christianization'"[3]. January 1888 C0065 The Bohdan Khmelnytsky Monument (1888) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government On the pedestal of the Khmelnytsky monument (1888) the empire cast a programmatic statement about the past: on the front side stood the phrase "We will to be under the tsar of the east, the Orthodox one," attributed to the Pereiaslav Rada, and on the right - the imperial formula "To Bohdan Khmelnytsky – one and indivisible Russia"[4]. Brought together, they presented the events of 1654 as a voluntary and final choice in favor of a single Russian state, and the entire history of the Hetmanate as the road to that choice. January 1933 C0079 Cultural Terror and the "Executed Renaissance" (1933–1938) G0010 USSR S0021 Propaganda The construction of a new Soviet-imperial historical canon to supplant the Ukrainian past: "from the late 1930s a thesis took hold in the historical scholarship of the USSR," proclaimed in the works of B. Grekov, K. Huslystyi, and F. Yastrebov, "of Kyivan Rus as the 'common cradle' of the history of the Ukrainian, Russian, and Belarusian peoples," and "in 1939 B. Grekov advanced the proposition of the ethnic unity of the 'Rus people' in the era of Kyivan Rus"[5]. This scheme displaced M. Hrushevsky's conception and denied the independence of Ukraine's history. January 1954 C0087 The Ideological Campaign of the "300th Anniversary of Reunification" and the Transfer of Crimea (1954) G0010 USSR S0021 Propaganda A state campaign to construct a historical myth: the "Theses on the 300th Anniversary of the Reunification of Ukraine with Russia," approved by the CPSU Central Committee, declared that "by this historic act was completed the long struggle of the freedom-loving Ukrainian people against foreign enslavers for reunification with the Russian people in a single Russian state"[6] – the annexation of 1654 was retroactively rewritten as the goal and outcome of a national struggle. January 2020 C0102 Ideological Preparation for the Full-Scale Invasion (2020–2021) G0011 Russian Federation S0009 Diplomacy The publication of the manifesto "On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians" (July 2021), constructing a pseudo-historical myth: "Russians and Ukrainians are one people, a single whole," while modern borders are declared the result of the fact that "the Bolsheviks' actions in severing from Russia its historical territories are not considered a criminal act"[7]. The same article describes how Lenin personally "persuaded" the leaders of the Donetsk-Kryvyi Rih republic "to act within Soviet Ukraine," and how the Central Committee resolved "to create at the congress 'one government for all of Ukraine'"[7]. On the eve of the invasion the thesis was taken to its limit: in his address of February 21, 2022 Putin declared that "modern Ukraine was entirely and wholly created by Russia, or, to be more precise, by Bolshevik, communist Russia," and called the country "Ukraine named after Vladimir Ilyich Lenin" - "He is its author and architect"[8]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Michael Khodarkovsky. Михайло Брайчевський (написано 1966, вид. Торонто: Нові дні, 1972; цитує «Тези до 300-річчя возз'єднання України з Росією», Київ, 1954). (1972). Приєднання чи возз'єднання?. В. Путин, kremlin.ru, 12 июля 2021. (2021). Статья Владимира Путина «Об историческом единстве русских и украинцев». В. Путин, kremlin.ru, 21 февраля 2022. (2022). title: Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority, technique T0003
content: Cultivation of a Logic of Superiority Aggressors may conduct systematic ideological indoctrination of their own population, cultivating a cult of exceptionalism and messianism. Within this paradigm, the colonizer's culture is proclaimed superior and a bearer of progress, while the culture of the colonized peoples is deliberately marginalized and portrayed as backward, derivative, or altogether lacking the right to independent existence. This serves as the basic ideological justification for subsequent domination. ID: T0003 ⓘ Tactic: Legitimization of Domination ⓘ Peoples: Nokhchi (Chechens), Ukrainians Contributors: decolonial.ist project Version: 1.1 Created: 21 April 2026 Last Modified: 9 August 2026 Discuss on Telegram Procedures Carried Out Text search (name, technique or description): Filter by peoples: Date range (by start): — Sort by date: January 1800 C1106 Propagandistic Inversion of Roles and Dehumanization (1800–1864) G0009 Russian Empire S0021 Propaganda The propaganda apparatus of the Russian Empire used poetry to broadcast the logic of domination into society: the imperial historian and participant in the events V. A. Potto records that the poet A. S. Pushkin proclaimed in verse the inevitability of subjugation: «Submit, Caucasus - Yermolov is coming!»[1], while the poet V. A. Zhukovsky extolled the destruction of infrastructure by military commanders: «Scarcely at the villages - the villages blaze»[2]. January 1864 C0063 Formation of the Ideology of Great-Power Chauvinism (1864–1876) G0009 Russian Empire S0008 Government The systematic imposition of the metropole's logic of superiority. Researchers reconstruct Katkov's logic thus: "a nation must be a tribe capable of creating a state; only a state nation can establish order in a given territory; tribes incapable of creating a state have to submit to the state nation"[3]. Katkov himself wrote: "In the recognition of a nation the question of power, of government, of the state is decided"[3]. Hrushevsky records both the thesis and its reach: Valuev invoked an imaginary "majority of Little Russians" who allegedly "know neither a Ukrainian nationality nor language, only one Russian people and tongue," while the ideology's mouthpieces carried it to the formula "there are no Ruthenians — there is only one 'Russian people' from the Carpathians to Kamchatka"[4]. January 2020 C0102 Ideological Preparation for the Full-Scale Invasion (2020–2021) G0011 Russian Federation S0021 Propaganda Total indoctrination of Russian society with the ideas of the philosopher I. Ilyin (so-called "white fascism") and the transformation of the "Russian World" concept into a state ideology (rashism) that justifies the metropole's cultural superiority and existential right to violence against its neighbors[5]. document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initProcedureList(document.getElementById("techProcs")); }); document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => { // пришли с матрицы конкретного народа — оставляем в фильтре только его // (чекбоксы уже построены initProcedureList: его DOMContentLoaded // зарегистрирован раньше и выполняется первым) const PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH = { "russia/ukrainians": "Ukrainians", "russia/nokhchi": "Nokhchi (Chechens)", }; const container = document.querySelector('#techProcs .people-filter-box'); if (!container) return; const ref = document.referrer || ""; for (const [path, people] of Object.entries(PEOPLE_BY_MATRIX_PATH)) { if (ref.includes('/matrices/' + path)) { const boxes = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]')); const target = boxes.find(cb => cb.value === people.toLowerCase()); if (target) { boxes.forEach(cb => { cb.checked = (cb === target); }); container.dispatchEvent(new Event('change')); } break; } } }); References Потто В..
